definition_zh: 暴力；暴行；猛烈
definition_en: behaviour meant to hurt or kill people, or great force in nature or feeling
core_image: 街角围起的人群，地上散落的碎玻璃
scene: 深夜的街角围起了警戒线，地上散着碎玻璃，警察在记录现场。 The city has seen a rise in violence since the summer.
sceneCN: 这里 violence 是「暴力」（第 1 个义项：意图伤害或杀害他人的行为）；句意为入夏以来这座城市的暴力事件增多了。街角围着的人群与碎玻璃正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 同源形容词，义为「暴力的；猛烈的」
加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「猛烈地」
同源动词，义为「违反；侵犯」

senses.title: Behaviour meant to hurt people
senses.definition: actions intended to injure, damage, or kill
senses.definitionCN: 意图伤害、破坏或杀害他人的行为
senses.example: The city has seen a rise in violence since the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 入夏以来这座城市的暴力事件增多了。
senses.why: From Latin violentia, the word names force pushed to the point of harm.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自拉丁语 violentia，指被推到伤害程度的力量。

senses.title: Great force in nature
senses.definition: the destructive power of storms, earthquakes, or other natural forces
senses.definitionCN: 风暴、地震等自然力量造成的破坏力
senses.example: The violence of the storm tore roofs from houses.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴之猛把房顶都掀了下来。
senses.why: Nature uses no fists, yet a storm’s force is spoken of with the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 自然并没有拳头，但风暴的力量用的仍是这个词。

senses.title: Intensity of feeling or expression
senses.definition: extreme force in emotion, words, or action
senses.definitionCN: 情感、言辞或行为上的极端强度
senses.example: She spoke with a violence that surprised her friends.
senses.exampleCN: 她说话之激烈让朋友们吃了一惊。
senses.why: Feelings can press as hard as hands, so intensity of speech borrows the word of blows.
senses.whyCN: 情绪能像手一样用力，于是言语的激烈借用了拳头的说法。

senses.title: Unlawful force in law
senses.definition: the use of physical force against a person or property contrary to law
senses.definitionCN: 对人身或财产非法使用的物理强制
senses.example: The charge was robbery with violence.
senses.exampleCN: 罪名是暴力抢劫。
senses.why: Courts need a precise term for force that breaks the law, and violence supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 法院需要一个精确术语指违法的强制，violence 正好胜任。

senses.title: In media, images of fighting and cruelty
senses.definition: shown fighting, killing, or cruelty in films and games
senses.definitionCN: 影视与游戏中展示的打斗、杀戮或残忍
senses.example: Parents asked for less violence in the evening schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 家长要求在晚间节目里少放暴力内容。
senses.why: Once screens show the act, the noun names the content as well as the deed.
senses.whyCN: 屏幕一旦展示这种行为，这个词既指行为，也指内容。

intro.en: Violence goes back to Latin violentia, from vis, force.
intro.cn: violence 追溯至拉丁语 violentia，源自 vis（力量）。

items.en: Vis meant force or power, and violentia named the quality of using it hard.
items.cn: vis 意为力量或强力，violentia 指蛮横使用力量的性质。

items.en: Violare, to treat with force, shares the same root.
items.cn: violare（施暴、亵渎）与它同根。

items.en: French violence carried the noun into English law and letters.
items.cn: 法语 violence 把这一名词带进英语的法律与文章。

items.en: English used it first for unlawful force.
items.cn: 中世纪英语先用它指非法强制。

items.en: Storms, feelings, and screen content took the word far beyond the courtroom.
items.cn: 风暴、情感与屏幕内容把这个词带出了法庭。

note.en: The first group holds the violence family, the second the words for force, fighting, and calm.
note.cn: 第一组是 violence 词族，第二组是力量、打斗与平静的相关词。

entries.definition: using force to hurt
entries.definitionCN: 暴力的；猛烈的

entries.definition: with great force
entries.definitionCN: 猛烈地

entries.definition: to break or invade
entries.definitionCN: 违反；侵犯

entries.definition: the act of breaking a rule
entries.definitionCN: 违反

entries.definition: strength used on a person or thing
entries.definitionCN: 武力；力量

entries.definition: cruel and savage treatment
entries.definitionCN: 野蛮；残暴

entries.definition: a serious disagreement or fight
entries.definitionCN: 冲突

entries.definition: the absence of fighting
entries.definitionCN: 和平

normalIntro.en: The root vis, force, fills the word: violence is force taken too far.
normalIntro.cn: 词根 vis（力量）贯穿全词：暴力就是把力量用过了头。

normal.en: Violet and violence look alike; only the ending differs.
normal.cn: violet 与 violence 形近，只差词尾。

normal.en: Violence ends in -ence, like patience.
normal.cn: violence 以 -ence 结尾，如同 patience。

normal.en: The adjective drops -nce for -nt: violent.
normal.cn: 形容词把 -nce 换成 -nt：violent。

normal.en: Resort to violence is a fixed phrase for turning to force.
normal.cn: 诉诸暴力常说 resort to violence。

normal.en: The stress falls on the first syllable: VI-o-lence.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节：VI-o-lence。

abstract.en: See broken glass on a corner at night.
abstract.cn: 想夜里街角的碎玻璃。

abstract.en: Hear a window shake as the storm hits.
abstract.cn: 听风暴来时的窗玻璃作响。

abstract.en: Picture a hand clenched over a table.
abstract.cn: 想桌子上一只攥紧的手。

examples.en: The report calls for an end to violence in the home.
examples.cn: 这份报告呼吁终止家庭暴力。

examples.en: No cause justifies the use of violence.
examples.cn: 任何理由都不能为使用暴力开脱。

examples.en: The violence of the waves kept the boats in port.
examples.cn: 浪势太猛，船都留在了港里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外来冷死」——外来的人被打得冷死在街头，这桩暴力令人心惊。

root: 拉丁语 vis（力量）→ violentia（强暴）→ 古法语 violence → 英语 violence

sensesIntro.en: Force used against people becomes the force of storms, of speech, of law, and of what screens show.
sensesIntro.cn: 用在人身上的力量，进而变成风暴之力、言语之力、法律上的强制与屏幕上的内容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a police line around broken glass at night.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜里警戒线围住的碎玻璃。

branches.en: The street branch: more attacks since summer.
branches.cn: 街头分支：入夏后袭击增多。

branches.en: The storm branch: roofs torn away.
branches.cn: 风暴分支：房顶被掀掉。

branches.en: The voice branch: a tone that startles friends.
branches.cn: 语气分支：让朋友吃惊的激烈语调。

branches.en: The court branch: a charge of robbery with force.
branches.cn: 法庭分支：暴力抢劫的罪名。

branches.en: The screen branch: parents ask for less of it.
branches.cn: 屏幕分支：家长要求少放暴力。

intro.en: The root viol-, from Latin vis, force, builds violence, violent, violate, and violation.
intro.cn: 词根 viol- 源自拉丁语 vis（力量），构成 violence、violent、violate、violation。

latinIntro.en: Latin vis, force, gives violentia; the -ence ending marks an abstract noun, as in patience.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vis（力量）派生 violentia；-ence 词尾标记抽象名词，如同 patience。

items.example: Viol- carries the sense of force.
Violence names the state of using force.
items.exampleCN: violence 指使用力量的状态。

items.example: Violate means to break with force.
A violation of the rule was reported.
items.exampleCN: 有人举报了违反规则之事。

items.example: Force is the plain word behind vis.
items.exampleCN: force 是 vis 背后的平实说法。
和平正是暴力所破坏的。

items.example: Violet shares the start but not the root.
items.exampleCN: violet 与它开头相同而词根不同。

definition_zh: 合乎逻辑的；合理的；逻辑学的；条理清楚的
definition_en: following the rules of valid inference, or sensible and well ordered
core_image: 黑板上每一步都从上一行推出，写完最后一行时，结论已经无处可躲
scene: 数学教室的黑板上，老师把条件一行行写下去，最后一行还没落笔，后排已经有学生点头。 The argument was logical at every step, so the conclusion seemed unavoidable.
sceneCN: 这里 logical 指「每一步都由前一步合法推出」（第 1 个义项：合乎有效推理）；句意为这个论证每一步都合乎逻辑，所以结论显得无法回避；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 合乎逻辑的；合理的；逻辑学的；有条理的

derivatives.zh: 逻辑；逻辑学（希腊词根「言辞、理性」，由「说话」转为「推理规则」）
逻辑上；必然地（形容词加副词后缀）
逻辑学家（名词词干加表从业者的后缀）
合乎逻辑的性质（形容词加名词后缀）

senses.title: Following valid inference
senses.definition: arranged so that each step is licensed by the rules of inference
senses.definitionCN: 安排得使每一步都由推理规则许可
senses.example: The argument was logical at every step, so the conclusion seemed unavoidable.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论证每一步都合乎逻辑，所以结论显得无法回避。
senses.why: The Greek root means 'word' and 'reason at work', so the adjective first says that the arrangement follows reason's rules.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根意为「言辞」与「运作中的理性」，因此这个形容词首先说明安排合乎理性的规则。

senses.title: Sensible and practical
senses.definition: being the choice or arrangement that a sensible person would make
senses.definitionCN: 是明理的人会作出的选择或安排
senses.example: Taking the earlier train was the logical thing to do.
senses.exampleCN: 坐早一班车才是合理的做法。
senses.why: Outside formal proof, valid inference is replaced by ordinary good judgment, and the word follows the looser use.
senses.whyCN: 在形式证明之外，有效推理被日常判断替代，这个词也随这种较松的用法走。

senses.title: Belonging to the discipline of logic
senses.definition: relating to logic as a formal subject of study
senses.definitionCN: 与作为正式研究科目的逻辑学相关
senses.example: A logical system needs rules for negation before it can do anything else.
senses.exampleCN: 一个逻辑系统先要有否定规则，才谈得上做别的。
senses.why: Once the discipline was named, its adjective began to describe the objects inside it.
senses.whyCN: 学科一旦被命名，它的形容词就开始描写学科内部的对象。

senses.title: Internally consistent
senses.definition: not contradicting itself, so that the parts can hold together
senses.definitionCN: 不自相矛盾，因此各部分能彼此撑住
senses.example: The account was logical but built on a false premise.
senses.exampleCN: 这套说法前后一致，却建立在一个假前提上。
senses.why: Consistency is the minimum that reasoning requires: no step may cancel an earlier one.
senses.whyCN: 自洽是推理的最低要求：任何一步都不能取消前面某一步。

senses.title: The expected next step
senses.definition: following so directly that it appears forced
senses.definitionCN: 接得如此直接，以致显得非如此不可
senses.example: Retirement was the logical end of a forty-year career.
senses.exampleCN: 退休是四十年职业生涯顺理成章的终点。
senses.why: When the chain is tight, the last link looks inevitable rather than chosen.
senses.whyCN: 当链条足够紧，最后一环看起来就不是选择，而是必然。

senses.title: Clear-headed as a person
senses.definition: describing a mind that proceeds in order and does not jump
senses.definitionCN: 形容心思按顺序推进、不跳跃
senses.example: She is a logical thinker even under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 即使在压力下，她也是思路清晰的思考者。
senses.why: The same quality that belongs to arguments is transferred to the people who make them.
senses.whyCN: 属于论证的性质被转移到制造论证的人身上。

senses.title: Of boolean operations in computing
senses.definition: in computing, describing operations on true and false values
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，形容对真值与假值进行的运算
senses.example: A logical error is often a single reversed condition.
senses.exampleCN: 逻辑运算上的错误常常只是一个条件写反了。
senses.why: Machines were built on the formal rules of inference, so the discipline's adjective became a technical label.
senses.whyCN: 机器建立在形式推理规则之上，于是这门学科的形容词成了技术标签。

senses.title: Ordered and methodical
senses.definition: laid out in an order where each part has a place
senses.definitionCN: 按某种次序排列，使每一部分各就其位
senses.example: Arrange the files in a logical order before the audit.
senses.exampleCN: 审计之前把文件按条理排好。
senses.why: Order is the visible trace of reasoning, even when no conclusion is being drawn.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有在得出结论，条理也是推理留下的可见痕迹。

intro.en: Logical comes from a Greek word for 'of speech or reason', which reached English through Latin and French. Its root treats speaking and reasoning as one act.
intro.cn: logical 来自希腊语中意为「属于言辞或理性的」的词，经拉丁语与法语进入英语。它的词根把说话与推理当作同一件事。

items.en: Logos meant 'word, speech, account, reason'. The same noun served for a sentence, a story, a ratio and the order of the world.
items.cn: logos 意为「词、言语、说明、理性」。同一个名词既可指一句话、一个故事、一个比值，也可指世界的秩序。

items.en: The verb behind the noun meant 'to say, to pick out, to gather'. Speech and selection share one root because speaking was seen as selecting words.
items.cn: 名词背后的动词意为「说、挑出、收集」。说话与选择共享一个词根，因为说话被视为在挑选词语。

items.en: The adjective meant 'skilled in speech or reasoning', and it named the art of argument rather than a branch of study.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为「擅长言辞或推理的」，它指论证的艺术，而不是一门学科。

items.en: Latin borrowed the adjective and the noun; Old French passed them to English, where the noun first named the art of arguing well.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该形容词与名词；古法语把它们传给英语，名词最初指善于论证的艺术。

items.en: As a taught subject, the noun settled into its modern sense, and the adjective came to describe whatever obeyed its rules.
items.cn: 作为被教授的科目，名词固定为现代意义，形容词则用来描写任何服从其规则的东西。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of the Greek verb is not established, and the reconstructed Indo-European root proposed for it is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个希腊动词的更早来源没有定论，为它提出的印欧词根属重构，只是假说。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same speech-and-reason root that are easy to confuse; the second holds near neighbours for being sensible or orderly.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「言辞与理性」词根、容易混淆的词；第二组是表示「明理」或「有条理」的近义词。

entries.definition: The discipline or the system of rules; the adjective describes what follows those rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科或规则体系；形容词则描写服从这些规则的东西。

entries.definition: From a Greek word for reckoning: it names the practical business of moving and supplying, not reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊语中指「计算」的词：指运输与补给的实际事务，而非推理。

entries.definition: One who studies the discipline, not something that conforms to it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究这门学科的人，而不是服从它的某物。

entries.definition: Built on the same noun with a prefix meaning 'according to': it names a comparison, not a rule of inference.
entries.definitionCN: 同一名词加意为「按照」的前缀：指比较，而非推理规则。

entries.definition: It adds a judgment about fairness or moderation, which logical does not contain.
entries.definitionCN: 多了对公平或适度的判断，而 logical 不含这一层。

entries.definition: It claims only that the parts do not clash, leaving open whether the whole is valid.
entries.definitionCN: 只声称各部分不冲突，至于整体是否有效则不论。

entries.definition: It praises a method followed throughout, even where the method itself is not logical.
entries.definitionCN: 称赞贯穿始终的方法，即使方法本身并不合乎逻辑。

entries.definition: In logic it means both correctly structured and built on true premises, a stronger claim than logical.
entries.definitionCN: 在逻辑中兼指结构正确与前提为真，比 logical 的主张更强。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Greek root means both 'word' and 'reason', so logical is about words that hold together by reason.
normal.cn: 希腊词根同时意为「言辞」与「理性」，所以 logical 说的是靠理性站得住的话。

normal.en: The family runs logic, logical, logically, logician, logicalness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 logic、logical、logically、logician、logicalness。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the chain: a logical step, a logical conclusion, a logical order.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出链条：合乎逻辑的一步、合乎逻辑的结论、逻辑顺序。

normal.en: The same root appears in words for dialogue, analogy and catalogue, all built on speech or gathering.
normal.cn: 同一个词根还出现在表示对话、类比与目录的词里，都由「说话」或「收集」构成。

normal.en: Computing uses the word for operations on true and false, because machines run on these rules.
normal.cn: 计算机领域用这个词指对真假的运算，因为机器就运行在这些规则上。

abstract.en: Picture a row of dominoes standing close enough that the first one settles the last.
abstract.cn: 想象一排立着的多米诺，近得第一张就能决定最后一张。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase with no missing step and no extra one.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯，既没有缺一阶，也没有多一阶。

abstract.en: Picture two maps of the same city that agree on every street.
abstract.cn: 想象同一座城市的两张地图，每条街都对得上。

examples.en: The logical conclusion of the policy is higher taxes.
examples.cn: 这项政策合乎逻辑的结论是更高的税。

examples.en: Her explanation was logical, but it began from a wrong assumption.
examples.cn: 她的解释合乎逻辑，但出发点是错的假设。

examples.en: Put the chapters in a logical order before you submit.
examples.cn: 交稿前把各章按逻辑顺序排好。

dict_mnemonic.text: log（言辞、理性）+ ical（属于……的）＝ 属于理性规则的 → 合乎逻辑的、合理的。

root: 希腊 logikos「擅长言辞或推理的」，来自 logos「词、言语、说明、理性」，其背后的动词 legein 意为「说、挑出、收集」；更深来源不确定。经拉丁与古法语进入英语。同族有 logic、logician、dialogue、analogy。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one chain of steps. It can be a formal derivation, a sensible choice, a branch of study, a self-consistent whole, the step that seems forced, the mind that keeps order, a machine's operation on true and false, or simply an arrangement with a place for everything.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条步骤链展开。它可以是形式推导、明智的选择、一门学科、自洽的整体、显得非如此不可的一步、保持次序的心智、机器对真假的运算，或仅仅是各得其所的排列。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain in which every link is fastened to the one before.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条每一环都扣在前一环上的链。

branches.en: RULE AND DISCIPLINE: the valid step, then the subject that studies such steps.
branches.cn: 规则与学科：有效的一步，以及研究这类步骤的科目。

branches.en: OUTSIDE THE PROOF: the same approval given to ordinary good judgment.
branches.cn: 走出证明之外：同样的认可被给了日常的明智判断。

branches.en: COHERENCE AND LAYOUT: parts that do not cancel each other, shown as a visible order.
branches.cn: 自洽与排布：彼此不取消的部分，显现为可见的次序。

branches.en: THE LAST LINK: the step that looks forced rather than chosen.
branches.cn: 最后一环：看起来不是被选择、而是被逼出的那一步。

branches.en: KEEPER AND MACHINE: the person whose thinking keeps order, and the circuit that runs on the same rules.
branches.cn: 守序者与机器：思维保持次序的人，以及运行在同样规则上的电路。

intro.en: Logical is a Greek-derived adjective carrying a Latin adjective ending, and the root behind it builds a large family in English.
intro.cn: logical 是一个源自希腊语的形容词，带着拉丁形容词词尾，它背后的词根在英语中构成一大批词。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplied the noun for word and reason; Latin and French supplied the endings that turned it into the English adjective and its relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供了指「言辞与理性」的名词；拉丁语与法语提供了把它变成英语形容词及其亲属的词尾。

items.example: One noun covers a sentence and the order of the world.
items.exampleCN: 一个名词同时涵盖一句话与世界的秩序。

items.structure: legein (Greek verb, 'to say, gather, pick out')
items.example: Speaking is pictured as picking words out.
items.exampleCN: 说话被描绘为把词挑出来。

items.example: The ending makes an adjective of skill.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾造出表示「擅长」的形容词。

items.example: Logic supplies the rules that reasoning follows.
items.exampleCN: 逻辑提供推理所遵循的规则。

items.example: The argument was logical at every step.
items.exampleCN: 这个论证每一步都合乎逻辑。

items.example: The two claims cannot both be true logically.
items.exampleCN: 这两个主张在逻辑上不可能同时为真。

items.example: A logician tests the form, not the content.
items.exampleCN: 逻辑学家检验形式，而非内容。

items.example: The prefix means 'across', so speech passes between two.
items.exampleCN: 前缀意为「穿过」，言语在两人之间往返。

items.example: The prefix means 'according to', giving a matching of ratios.
items.exampleCN: 前缀意为「按照」，给出比值的对应。

items.example: The ending names disciplines built on ordered speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾命名建立在有序言说之上的学科。

derivatives.zh: 逻辑；逻辑学（希腊词根「言辞、理性」，由「说话」转为「推理规则」）
逻辑上；必然地（形容词加副词后缀）
逻辑学家（名词词干加表从业者的后缀）
合乎逻辑的性质（形容词加名词后缀）

definition_zh: 多数；大多数；多数票；议会多数派；法定成年
definition_en: the larger part of a group, the winning margin in a vote, the larger bloc in a legislature, and the age at which a person becomes legally adult
core_image: 人群沿一条线站开，超过半数的人站到同一边，把另一边挡住
scene: 选举结果还没贴出，镇公所外的长椅上已经坐满了等候的人。 The majority of the town had gathered outside the hall before the count was read.
sceneCN: 这里是「多数、大多数」（第 1 个义项：人数较多的那一部分）；句意为票数宣读之前，镇上大多数人已经聚在会堂外。

pos.zh: 多数；大多数；多数票；议会多数派；法定成年

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语比较级 maior 直接借入，义为「主要的；专业」
由 majority 加 -arian 构成，义为「多数主义的；多数主义者」
由 majoritarian 加 -ism 构成，义为「多数主义；多数统治论」

senses.title: The larger part of a group
senses.definition: the part of a group that is larger than the other parts
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中比其余部分更大的那一部分
senses.example: The majority of the students chose the morning class.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数学生选了上午的课。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin maior, the comparative of magnus, so its core idea is simply the bigger of two shares.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语 maior，是 magnus 的比较级，所以核心念头就是两份当中更大的那一份。

senses.title: The winning margin in a vote
senses.definition: the difference in votes by which one candidate or side defeats the other
senses.definitionCN: 一个候选人或一方击败另一方时所领先的票数之差
senses.example: She won by a majority of sixty votes.
senses.exampleCN: 她以六十票的优势获胜。
senses.why: Counting turns larger shares into figures, and once the larger share decides a contest it becomes a margin of victory.
senses.whyCN: 计票把较大的份额换算成数字，而一旦较大的份额决出胜负，它就成了胜选的优势票数。

senses.title: The larger bloc in a legislature
senses.definition: the party or group that holds more seats than its opponents in a legislature
senses.definitionCN: 在议会中比对手占有更多席位的政党或团体
senses.example: The majority pushed the bill through both houses.
senses.exampleCN: 多数派推动这项议案在两院都获得通过。
senses.why: Where votes decide seats, the winning share hardens into a standing bloc, and the comparative idea becomes a body with power.
senses.whyCN: 在按票数分配席位的场合，获胜的份额凝固成一个常设阵营，比较的概念由此变成一个握有权力的团体。

senses.title: The age of legal adulthood
senses.definition: the age at which a person is legally treated as an adult
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在法律上被当作成年人的年龄
senses.example: In that country a person reaches the age of majority at eighteen.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个国家，人到十八岁就达到法定成年年龄。
senses.why: A young person who has lived through the greater number of childhood years steps into full legal rights, so the same idea of the greater share marks the passage into adulthood.
senses.whyCN: 一个年轻人度过较多的童年岁月之后迈入完整的法律权利，同一个「较大份额」的概念便被用来标志成年。

intro.en: Majority is built from the Latin comparative maior, greater, and the noun ending -itas, and English first used it for superiority before it settled on numbers.
intro.cn: majority 由拉丁语比较级 maior（更大的）加名词词尾 -itas 构成；英语最初用它表示优越，之后才固定到数量上。

items.en: Magnus meant great or large, and its comparative maior meant greater.
items.cn: magnus 意为大的、伟大的，它的比较级 maior 意为更大的。

items.en: Maior, also written major, supplied the adjective for the larger of two shares.
items.cn: maior 也写作 major，用来指两份之中较大的那一份。

items.en: The abstract noun maioritas named the state of being greater, and French carried it onward as majorite.
items.cn: 抽象名词 maioritas 指「更大的状态」，法语又把它作为 majorite 继续传下去。

items.en: Early English majority meant superiority or precedence before it was applied to the greater number of votes or people.
items.cn: 早期的英语 majority 先表示优越、优先，之后才用于指较多的票数或人数。

items.en: Modern English extends the noun to election margins, parliamentary blocs and the legal age of adulthood.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个名词扩展到选举票差、议会多数派以及法定成年年龄。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin comparative maior and the root magnus; the near-meaning group gathers words for the greatest share and the winning side.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁比较级 maior 与词根 magnus 上的词；近义组收表示最大份额与获胜一方的词。

entries.definition: The adjective and noun that share the Latin comparative maior with majority.
entries.definitionCN: 与 majority 同出拉丁比较级 maior 的形容词与名词。

entries.definition: Favouring decisions by the majority, built from majority plus -arian.
entries.definitionCN: 主张由多数人作决定，由 majority 加 -arian 构成。

entries.definition: Size or extent, from the same magnus root but with a different ending.
entries.definitionCN: 大小、程度，同出 magnus 词根但词尾不同。

entries.definition: The greatest possible amount, from the superlative of magnus.
entries.definitionCN: 可能的最大量，来自 magnus 的最高级。

entries.definition: The greatest number or part of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物中数量或部分最大的。

entries.definition: The main or larger part of something, especially a group.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物、尤指人群的主要或较大部分。

entries.definition: The largest number of votes when no one reaches a majority.
entries.definitionCN: 无人过半时得票最多的票数；相对多数。

entries.definition: A superiority in number or weight.
entries.definitionCN: 在数量或分量上的优势。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin comparative turned into a noun, and its branches all measure one thing against another: shares, votes, seats and years.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把拉丁比较级变成名词，它的各条分支都在拿一件事与另一件事相比：份额、票数、席位与年岁。

normal.en: Majority starts with major, the Latin comparative for greater, so the word names the bigger share before it names anything political.
normal.cn: majority 开头就是 major，即拉丁语中表示「更大的」比较级，所以这个词先指较大的份额，之后才带上政治色彩。

normal.en: The ending -ity turns an adjective into a state, so majority is literally the state of being greater.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ity 把形容词变成状态名词，所以 majority 字面上就是「更大的状态」。

normal.en: In elections a majority means more than half, while a plurality means only more than anyone else; the two words should not be swapped.
normal.cn: 在选举里 majority 指超过半数，而 plurality 只指比其他人多；这两个词不能互换。

normal.en: The age of majority is the birthday when the law stops calling a person a child.
normal.cn: 法定成年年龄就是法律不再把某个人叫作孩子的那一个生日。

normal.en: Majority leader is a fixed title in legislatures, which is why majority can name a bloc and not only a number.
normal.cn: 多数党领袖是议会里的固定头衔，这也是 majority 能指一个阵营而不只是数字的原因。

abstract.en: Half a room standing on one side of a line: the moment the line is crossed, a crowd becomes a majority.
abstract.cn: 半屋子人站到线的同一侧：跨过这条线的那一刻，一群人就成了多数。

abstract.en: A tally sheet at midnight turns a crowd into a number, and a number into a winner.
abstract.cn: 午夜的一张计票单把人群变成数字，又把数字变成胜者。

abstract.en: Turning eighteen changes nothing in the body, yet the law suddenly calls the same person an adult.
abstract.cn: 满十八岁身体没有变化，法律却突然把同一个人叫作成年人。

examples.en: The majority of the students chose the morning class.
examples.cn: 大多数学生选了上午的课。

examples.en: She won by a majority of sixty votes.
examples.cn: 她以六十票的优势获胜。

examples.en: A two-thirds majority is required to change the constitution.
examples.cn: 修改宪法需要三分之二的多数票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马脚瑞梯」——多数人一起扶着一架马脚梯往上爬；记住 majority 是多数。

root: 拉丁语 magnus（大的）→ 比较级 maior（更大的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 maioritas（更大状态）→ 法语 majorite → 英语 majority；同族词多与「更大、主要」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the larger share of a group; the same comparison then yields a winning vote margin, a standing bloc in a legislature, and the legal age of adulthood.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一个群体里较大的那一份；同一个比较关系随后生出选举的胜选票差、议会中的常设阵营，以及法定成年年龄。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn across a crowd, with more than half the people standing on one side.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群中间画一条线，超过半数的人站在同一边。

branches.en: a crowd outnumbering everyone else in the square
branches.cn: 广场上人数压过其他所有人的一群

branches.en: a count that decides who takes the seat
branches.cn: 决定谁取得席位的票数统计

branches.en: the winning side sitting together in the chamber
branches.cn: 在议事厅里坐在一起的获胜一方

branches.en: a birthday that marks legal adulthood
branches.cn: 标志法定成年的生日

branches.en: one word for the larger part and for being old enough
branches.cn: 同一个词既指较大的部分，也指年纪够大

intro.en: The word is carried by the Latin comparative maior, the noun ending -itas, and a family of English forms built on both.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁比较级 maior、名词词尾 -itas，以及建立在这两者之上的一组英语形式共同承载。

latinIntro.en: Latin is the direct source here: magnus gave the comparative maior, and maioritas gave the abstract noun behind majority.
latinIntro.cn: 这里拉丁语是直接来源：magnus 给出比较级 maior，maioritas 则给出 majority 背后的抽象名词。

items.meaning: greater; main; a field of study
based on rule by the majority

latinEntries.meaning: the state of being greater; a larger part
latinEntries.meaningCN: 更大的状态；较大的部分

definition_zh: 真实的；确实的；真正的；忠实的
definition_en: matching the facts, real rather than imagined, or faithful to a person or a promise
core_image: 一把校准好的尺子与墙上标出的刻度严丝合缝
scene: 工作台上放着一根木尺，工匠把它贴到墙上核对刻度是否对得上。 Every word in his report proved to be true.
sceneCN: 这里 true 是「真实的；确实的」（第 1 个义项：与事实相符的）；句意为他报告中的每个字都被证明是真的。尺子贴墙核对刻度，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 true 加 -th 构成，义为「真相；真理」
由 true 加 -ly 构成，义为「真正地；真诚地」
由 truth 加 -ful 构成，义为「诚实的；真实的」

senses.title: Matching the facts
senses.definition: agreeing with what actually happened or exists
senses.definitionCN: 与实际发生或存在的情况相符
senses.example: Every word in his report proved to be true.
senses.exampleCN: 他报告中的每个字都被证明是真的。
senses.why: The old English word meant faithful and firm, and something faithful to the facts is simply true.
senses.whyCN: 古英语中这个词意为忠信、牢固，而忠于事实的东西自然就是真的。

senses.title: Real, not imitated
senses.definition: used of something that deserves its name completely
senses.definitionCN: 用于完全配得上其名称的事物
senses.example: This is a true copy of the original page.
senses.exampleCN: 这是原页的真实副本。
senses.why: If a copy keeps faith with the original, it can be called true, and so the word reached the sense of genuine.
senses.whyCN: 如果副本忠于原件，就能称作 true，于是这个词也延伸出「名副其实」的意思。

senses.title: Faithful to a person
senses.definition: staying loyal to a friend, a promise, or a cause
senses.definitionCN: 对朋友、承诺或事业保持忠诚
senses.example: A true friend tells you what you need to hear.
senses.exampleCN: 真正的朋友会说出你需要听的话。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, the fixed and steady heart that the old word first named.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：那个古词最初命名的是固定不移的心。

intro.en: True is one of the oldest English words, and its earliest sense was faithful or firm rather than factual.
intro.cn: true 是英语最古老的词之一，最早的意思是忠信、牢固，而不是「合乎事实」。

items.en: The Germanic root treuwaz named that which is firm, loyal, and trustworthy.
items.cn: 日耳曼语词根 treuwaz 指牢固、忠实、可信赖之物。

items.en: Old English treowe meant faithful to a lord or a promise.
items.cn: 古英语 treowe 意为对领主或承诺的忠信。

items.en: Middle English extended it to statements that keep faith with the facts.
items.cn: 中古英语把它扩展到与事实相符的陈述。

items.en: The adjective also took the sense of genuine, as in a true copy.
items.cn: 这个形容词也取得「真正的」意义，如 a true copy。

items.en: Come true and hold true keep the old idea of a thing staying firm.
items.cn: come true 与 hold true 保留了事物稳固不移的旧意。

note.en: The first group shares the tru stem, the second holds other words about accuracy and honesty.
note.cn: 第一组共享 tru 词干，第二组收其他表示准确与诚实的词。

entries.definition: That which agrees with the facts.
entries.definitionCN: 真相；真理

entries.definition: In a real and honest way.
entries.definitionCN: 真正地；真诚地

entries.definition: Telling the facts honestly.
entries.definitionCN: 诚实的；真实的

entries.definition: Correct in every detail.
entries.definitionCN: 准确的

entries.definition: Real and not a copy.
entries.definitionCN: 真正的；非伪造的

entries.definition: Staying loyal to a person or promise.
entries.definitionCN: 忠实的

normalIntro.en: True keeps the old idea of being firm and faithful, and facts are simply what a word stays faithful to.
normalIntro.cn: true 保留着「牢固、忠实」的古意，而事实不过是一个词所忠于的对象。

normal.en: The silent e drops before -ly: truly.
normal.cn: 加 -ly 前去掉不发音的 e：truly。

normal.en: True becomes truth with -th, like warm and warmth.
normal.cn: true 加 -th 变 truth，就像 warm 加 -th 变 warmth。

normal.en: Come true means the wish has become real.
normal.cn: come true 意为愿望成了真。

normal.en: The vowel is long, like the sound in food.
normal.cn: 元音是长音，像 food 里的音。

normal.en: Hold true means the rule still stands.
normal.cn: hold true 意为这条规则仍然成立。

abstract.en: A ruler laid along a wall and matching the marks exactly.
abstract.cn: 一把尺贴墙，与刻线完全对齐。

abstract.en: A promise kept long after everyone stopped watching.
abstract.cn: 没有人再看着时仍然守住的承诺。

abstract.en: A photograph and the face it shows, with no gap between.
abstract.cn: 一张照片与它呈现的脸，二者没有缝隙。

examples.en: It is true that the bridge was closed for a month.
examples.cn: 那座桥确实关闭了一个月。

examples.en: Her dream of seeing the sea finally came true.
examples.cn: 她看海的心愿终于实现了。

examples.en: He remained loyal to the original design in every detail.
examples.cn: 他在每个细节上都忠于最初的设计。

dict_mnemonic.text: true 与 tree 同源——像树一样笔直立着不动摇，就是真实、忠实。

root: 古英语 treowe（忠信、牢固），来自日耳曼语词根 treuwaz，与 tree、truth 同源；同族词有 truth、truly、truthful。

sensesIntro.en: First what agrees with the facts, then what is genuine, then the old sense of loyalty.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是与事实相符，再是名副其实，最后回到最古老的忠诚之义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler matching the marks exactly.
core.cn: 核心意象：尺子与刻线严丝合缝。

branches.en: The fact branch: words that agree with events.
branches.cn: 事实分支：与事件相符的话。

branches.en: The genuine branch: a thing worthy of its name.
branches.cn: 真品分支：配得上名字的东西。

branches.en: The loyalty branch: a heart that does not move.
branches.cn: 忠诚分支：不会动摇的心。

branches.en: The test branch: both are checked against a standard.
branches.cn: 检验分支：两者都要对照标准查。

branches.en: The old root branch: faithfulness and truth share one stem.
branches.cn: 古词根分支：忠信与真实共用一个词干。

intro.en: True is a short Germanic stem, and English builds truth and truly on it with two old endings.
intro.cn: true 是短小的日耳曼语词干，英语用两个古老词尾在上面造出 truth 与 truly。

latinIntro.en: No Latin ancestor exists for true; the Latin words below are distant cousins of the same idea.
latinIntro.cn: true 没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词只是同一概念的远亲。

items.example: The stem serves as the adjective itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干本身就是形容词。

items.example: It forms truth, the state of being true.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 truth，真实的状态。

items.example: It forms truly, in a true way.

items.exampleCN: 它由 truth 构成 truthful。

items.example: The noun names the fact itself.
The e drops before the suffix.
items.exampleCN: 加词尾前 e 要去掉。

definition_zh: 所有权；拥有；归属关系
definition_en: the state or legal right of possessing something, or the relation by which a thing belongs to a person
core_image: 一枚刻着名字的铜牌钉在门上，钥匙挂在旁边，名字在牌上的人就有权处置屋内之物
scene: 产权登记处把房屋过户到买方名下，登记簿上的名字一换，处置权随之转移。 The land registry transferred the house to the buyer, and once the name on the register changed, ownership passed with it.
sceneCN: 这里指「对某物享有法律上的所有权」，对应第 1 个义项：可以占有、使用与处置的权利；句意为登记簿上的名字一换，所有权随之转移。画面要点：门上的铜牌、挂着的钥匙、登记簿；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 所有权；拥有（不可数，常后接表示所属物的介词短语，指明所拥有之物）

derivatives.zh: 所有者；物主（动词加表施事的名词后缀，指对某物享有所有权的人）
共有人（表示「共同」的前缀与所有者一词复合，指与他人共享所有权的人）
共有；共同所有（表示「共同」的前缀与所有权一词复合，指所有权由多人分享）
拥有；承认（古英语动词，指对某物有支配权，后引申为「承认某事属于自己」）

senses.title: The legal right to dispose of a thing
senses.titleCN: 对物进行处置的法律权利
senses.definition: the legal power to use, sell, give away or exclude others from a thing
senses.definitionCN: 使用、出售、赠予某物并排除他人使用的法律权力
senses.example: The land registry transferred the house to the buyer, and once the name on the register changed, ownership passed with it.
senses.exampleCN: 产权登记处把房屋过户给买方，登记簿上的名字一换，所有权随之转移。
senses.why: The word joins the verb 'to have' to a suffix for a condition, so it names a state of having that the law will protect.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把表示「拥有」的动词与表状态的后缀结合，命名一种法律会保护的有有状态。

senses.title: Holding something in fact
senses.definition: the actual possession of a thing, whether or not the law recognises a title
senses.definitionCN: 实际持有某物，无论法律是否承认其权属
senses.example: Ownership of the keys does not always mean ownership of the flat.
senses.exampleCN: 拿着钥匙并不总意味着拥有这套公寓。
senses.why: Possession and title can come apart, and the word sometimes describes the plain fact of having rather than the right to have.
senses.whyCN: 占有与权属可以分开，这个词有时描述「手上确实有」这一事实，而不是「有权拥有」。

senses.title: The relation of belonging
senses.definition: the link by which a thing is attributed to a person, so that it answers to that person's name
senses.definitionCN: 某物被归到某人名下、对其名字作出回应的那种联系
senses.example: Ownership of the manuscript is disputed between two libraries.
senses.exampleCN: 这份手稿的归属在两家图书馆之间存有争议。
senses.why: Beyond the right and the fact lies a relation: the thing belongs to someone, and that belonging is what the noun most abstractly names.
senses.whyCN: 在权利与事实之外还有一层关系：物属于某人，而这种归属正是这个名词最抽象地命名的东西。

senses.title: Shareholding and proprietorship
senses.definition: the holding of shares in a company, or the position of a person who owns a firm
senses.definitionCN: 持有公司股份，或拥有某企业的业主地位
senses.example: Foreign ownership of the airline was capped at a fixed share.
senses.exampleCN: 该航空公司的外资持股被限定在固定比例内。
senses.why: When firms replace land as the main object of wealth, the same noun measures who holds the shares.
senses.whyCN: 当企业取代土地成为财富的主要对象，同一个名词就用来衡量谁持有股份。

senses.title: Public versus private regimes
senses.titleCN: 公有与私有的制度之分
senses.definition: the system under which the means of production or a service is held by the state or by private persons
senses.definitionCN: 生产资料或某项服务由国家持有还是由私人持有的制度安排
senses.example: The dispute was about ownership of the water supply, not about its price.
senses.exampleCN: 争论在于供水归谁所有，而不在于水价。
senses.why: Ownership becomes a political question once whole industries rather than single objects are at stake.
senses.whyCN: 一旦涉及的是整个行业而不是单件物品，所有权就成了政治问题。

senses.title: Personal responsibility for a task
senses.definition: the attitude of treating a problem or project as one's own, with the duty to see it through
senses.definitionCN: 把某个问题或项目当作自己的事、并承担完成责任的态度
senses.example: The team asked each member to take ownership of one part of the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 团队要求每位成员对计划的一部分负起责任。
senses.why: Modern management borrowed the legal word and stripped the title from it, leaving only the sense of treating the work as one's own.
senses.whyCN: 现代管理借用了这个法律词，抽去了权属，只留下「把工作当作自己的事」这一层。

senses.title: Attribution of a work to its author
senses.definition: the legal and moral link between a creative work and the person who made it
senses.definitionCN: 创造性作品与其创作者之间的法律与道义联系
senses.example: Ownership of the copyright passed to the publisher for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 著作权中的财产权在十年内转给了出版方。
senses.why: A text or a design can belong to someone too, so the noun extends from goods to works of the mind.
senses.whyCN: 文本或设计同样可以属于某人，因此这个名词从货物延伸到心智作品。

senses.title: Tenure of land in older law
senses.definition: the holding of land under a lord or a superior, with duties attached, rather than outright title
senses.definitionCN: 在领主或上级之下持有土地并附带义务，而不是绝对的所有权
senses.example: In that period ownership of land carried service as well as rent.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个时期，土地保有权既带来地租，也带来服役义务。
senses.why: Before absolute title was common, holding land meant holding it of someone, and the word recorded that layered relation.
senses.whyCN: 在绝对所有权普及之前，持有土地意味着从某人那里持有，这个词记录了那种分层的关系。

intro.en: Ownership joins the Old English verb agan 'to have, possess' to the suffix -ship, which came from a word for shape or condition. Both parts are Germanic, and the compound is a native English formation rather than a borrowing.
intro.cn: ownership 由古英语动词 agan「拥有、占有」加后缀 -ship 构成，而后缀出自一个表示「形状、状态」的词。两部分都属日耳曼语，这个复合词是英语本族造词，而不是借词。

items.en: Agan 'to have, to possess' is the verb behind own, and it is Germanic, with recorded relatives in other old Germanic languages.
items.cn: agan 意为「有、占有」，是 own 背后的动词，属日耳曼语，在其他古老日耳曼语言中有可考的同族词。

items.en: The reconstructed verb is posited with a star; the deeper Indo-European root is also a reconstruction, so the earliest layer is not directly attested.
items.cn: 重构的动词形式以带星号的方式拟出；更深的印欧语词根同样属重构，因此最早的层次没有直接文献实证。

items.en: The suffix came from a word meaning 'shape, condition', and it built nouns for states, offices and skills.
items.cn: 这个后缀出自一个表示「形状、状态」的词，用来构成表示状态、职位与技艺的名词。

items.en: The compound joined the two and named the condition of one who has something, at first in ordinary rather than legal language.
items.cn: 这个复合词把两者结合，命名「拥有某物者的状态」，最初用于日常语言而非法律语言。

items.en: Lawyers later separated ownership from mere holding, giving the noun a technical sense that possession alone does not fill.
items.cn: 法学家后来把所有权与单纯的占有分开，使这个名词获得一个单靠占有无法填补的专业含义。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word also came to mean personal responsibility for a task. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 在二十世纪，这个词也开始指对任务负起个人责任。年代为约数。

note.en: The first group is built from the same verb or looks close to it; the second group gives near alternatives from law, accounting and plain possession.
note.cn: 第一组由同一个动词构成或与它形近；第二组是来自法律、会计与日常占有三个方向的近义替代。

entries.definition: To possess, or belonging to oneself, as in one's own; it is the source word, while the entry noun names the relation.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有，或属于自己，如「自己的」；它是来源词，而本名词命名那种关系。

entries.definition: The person who holds title to a thing; the suffix marks a person, so the word cannot name the relation itself.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物持有权属的人；后缀标示人，因此这个词不能命名关系本身。

entries.definition: Still to be paid, as in an owing sum; it comes from the verb owe, which is a different word from own.
entries.definitionCN: 尚待支付的，如「欠款」；它出自动词「欠」，与「拥有」是不同的词。

entries.definition: A person who owns the home he lives in; it joins the owner word to a word for occupying.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有并居住在自己房屋的人；它把「所有者」与「占用」两个词连在一起。

entries.definition: The fact of having something under one's control; it can exist without legal title, which is why the two are distinguished.
entries.definitionCN: 某物处于控制之下的事实；它可以没有法律权属而存在，因此两者被区分开。

entries.definition: The status of an owner, especially of a business; it is close in meaning but more formal and more often used of firms.
entries.definitionCN: 所有人的身份，尤指企业所有人；它意思相近，但更正式，也更常用于企业。

entries.definition: The legal right to own property, or the document proving it; it is the lawyer's word for the proof rather than the relation.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有财产的合法权利，或证明它的文件；它是法学家用来指证明而非关系的词。

entries.definition: The care and control of a person or thing, often without ownership; a custodian may hold what belongs to another.
entries.definitionCN: 对人或在物的照管与控制，往往不含所有权；保管人可以持有属于他人之物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Old English verb for having, the native suffix for a condition, real derived words and real legal phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：古英语中表示「有」的动词、本族语中表状态的后缀、真实派生词与真实法律用语。

normal.en: The core is a name on a door: the thing answers to that name.
normal.cn: 核心是门上刻着的一个名字：那件东西对那个名字作出回应。

normal.en: The family runs own, owner, owners and co-ownership.
normal.cn: 同族词包括拥有、所有者、各位所有者与共有。

normal.en: Law separates the right from the holding, which is why possession alone is not ownership.
normal.cn: 法律把权利与占有分开，所以单有占有并不构成所有权。

normal.en: A company can be owned as surely as a field, so the word measures shares as well as soil.
normal.cn: 公司可以像田地一样被拥有，因此这个词既衡量股份，也衡量土地。

normal.en: Modern managers ask staff to take ownership of a problem, which keeps only the sense of treating it as one's own.
normal.cn: 现代管理者要求员工对问题「负起责任」，这里只保留了「把它当作自己的事」这一层。

abstract.en: Picture a brass plate on a door with a name cut into it, and a key hanging from the same hook.
abstract.cn: 想象门上钉着一块刻了名字的铜牌，同一只钩子上挂着钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture a register whose page is rewritten, and the right to the house moving with the ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一本登记簿的页面被改写，房屋的权利随墨迹一起转移。

abstract.en: Picture a worker who writes his own name on a task that no one assigned to him.
abstract.cn: 想象一名工人把名字写在一件没有人指派给他的任务上。

examples.en: Ownership of the building was split between two families.
examples.cn: 这栋楼的所有权由两户人家分有。

examples.en: The report recommends wider home ownership among younger households.
examples.cn: 报告建议让更多年轻家庭拥有自有住房。

examples.en: She took ownership of the delay and explained what went wrong.
examples.cn: 她承担了延误的责任，并解释了出错之处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧呢事普」——「欧」听成「我」，「呢」听成「的」：写着我的名字的那件东西，就是所有权。

root: 古英语 agan「拥有、占有」+ 古英语 -scipe「形状、状态」→ ownership。两部分均属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语来源；该动词的日耳曼语祖形与更深的印欧语词根都属重构形式，无直接文献实证。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings start from a name on a door. The legal right to dispose comes first, then the plain fact of holding, then belonging as a relation; from there the word measures shares, divides public from private regimes, lends itself to personal responsibility, extends to works of the mind, and remembers an older layered tenure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从门上刻着的名字开始。先是对物处置的法律权利，其次是持有的事实，再其次是归属这一关系；由此这个词衡量股份、区分公有与私有、借给个人责任感、延伸到心智作品，并记得一种较早的分层保有权。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name on a plate beside a key, marking who may dispose of what is behind the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙旁铜牌上的名字，标明谁有权处置门后之物。

branches.en: RIGHT AND HOLDING: the legal power to dispose, and the bare fact of having something in hand.
branches.cn: 权利与持有：处置的法律权力，以及手中确实有某物的事实。

branches.en: BELONGING: the relation that ties a thing to a name, including the older layered tenure of land.
branches.cn: 归属：把物与名字系在一起的关系，包括较早的分层土地保有权。

branches.en: SHARES: ownership measured in stock, and the position of a firm's proprietor.
branches.cn: 股份：以股票衡量的所有权，以及企业业主的地位。

branches.en: REGIMES: the political division between public and private holding.
branches.cn: 制度：公有与私有之间的政治分野。

branches.en: RESPONSIBILITY AND AUTHORSHIP: treating a task as one's own, and attributing a work to its maker.
branches.cn: 责任与作者身份：把任务当作自己的事，以及把作品归到创作者名下。

intro.en: This family is entirely Germanic: a verb for having plus a native suffix for a condition, with compounds built by adding person and place words.
intro.cn: 这个家族完全是日耳曼语的：一个表示「拥有」的动词，加上一个本族语的表状态后缀，再由表示人与处所的词构成复合形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this family. Latin-based near synonyms such as possession and proprietorship come from different roots.
latinIntro.cn: 这个家族没有拉丁语来源。由拉丁语派生的近义词如「占有」与「所有权」出自不同的词根。

items.meaning: the condition of holding something as one's own
items.meaningCN: 把某物作为自己之物持有的状态
items.example: Ownership passed to the buyer on signature.
items.exampleCN: 签署之时所有权转移给买方。

items.example: They own the land beside the river.
The owners met to divide the rent.
items.exampleCN: 各位业主开会分配租金。

items.meaning: a holder of title shared with another
items.example: Each co-owner may use the whole garden.
items.exampleCN: 每位共有人都可以使用整个花园。

items.meaning: title shared by more than one person
items.exampleCN: 共有要求就修缮达成一致。

items.example: The landowner leased the field for ten years.
items.exampleCN: 地主把这块田租了十年。

items.meaning: a person who owns the house he lives in
items.example: Homeowners pay a local property tax.
items.exampleCN: 房主需缴纳地方房产税。

derivatives.zh: 所有者；物主（动词加表施事的名词后缀，指对某物享有所有权的人）
共有人（表示「共同」的前缀与所有者一词复合，指与他人共享所有权的人）
共有；共同所有（表示「共同」的前缀与所有权一词复合，指所有权由多人分享）
拥有；承认（古英语动词，指对某物有支配权，后引申为「承认某事属于自己」）

definition_zh: 难以置信的；惊人的；极好的
definition_en: too strange or extreme to be believed, or extremely good
core_image: 听见一句话，眉毛先跳起来，嘴还没张开
scene: 朋友说自己一夜游过海峡，你第一反应是不信。 It sounds incredible, but she finished the race in under three hours.
sceneCN: 这里 incredible 是「难以置信的」（第 1 个义项：难以相信）；句意是听起来难以置信，但她不到三小时就跑完了全程。

pos.zh: 形容词：难以置信的；惊人的；极好的

derivatives.zh: 义为「难以置信地；极其」，由本词加 -ly 构成
义为「可信的」，去掉 in- 即成肯定形式
义为「信任、信用」，与本词同根
义为「可信度」

senses.title: Too strange to believe
senses.titleCN: 难以置信：奇怪到无法相信
senses.definition: so unusual or extreme that it is hard to believe
senses.definitionCN: 极其反常或极端，令人难信
senses.example: It sounds incredible, but she finished the race in under three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 听起来难以置信，但她不到三小时就跑完了全程。
senses.why: The Latin credere means to believe, and the negative prefix in- says no: not to be believed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 credere 意为「相信」，否定前缀 in- 说「不」：不可被相信。

senses.title: Extremely large or great
senses.titleCN: 惊人的：规模或程度极大
senses.definition: so great in size or amount that it surprises the mind
senses.definitionCN: 在规模或数量上大到让人吃惊
senses.example: The team worked at incredible speed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队以惊人的速度工作。
senses.why: When a number passes belief, the same word measures size rather than truth.
senses.whyCN: 当一个数字超出相信的范围，同一个词就转而衡量大小而非真伪。

senses.title: Extremely good, in speech
senses.definition: used informally to praise something as wonderful
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用来称赞某物好极了
senses.example: The view from the top was incredible.
senses.exampleCN: 山顶的景色美极了。
senses.why: Praise borrows the same exclamation: what is beyond belief is also beyond the ordinary.
senses.whyCN: 赞叹借用了同一句惊叹：超出相信的，也超出寻常。

senses.title: Hard to accept, used of behaviour
senses.titleCN: 难以接受：形容行为过分
senses.definition: used of behaviour that seems shockingly unfair or careless
senses.definitionCN: 形容行为不公或粗心到令人震惊
senses.example: It is incredible that they left the door unlocked.
senses.exampleCN: 他们竟没锁门，真让人难以接受。
senses.why: The negative prefix carries moral weight too: such conduct should not be believed of anyone.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀也带道德分量：这种行为不该被相信会出自任何人。

intro.en: Incredible comes from Latin incredibilis, from in-, not, and credere, to believe.
intro.cn: incredible 来自拉丁语 incredibilis，由 in-（不）与 credere（相信）构成。

items.en: Credere meant to trust or to entrust, the source of credit and creed.
items.cn: credere 意为「信任、托付」，是 credit 与 creed 的来源。

items.en: Incredibilis named what could not be believed, often of marvels.
items.cn: incredibilis 指令人无法相信之事，常用于奇闻。

items.en: English borrowed it through French for tales that defied belief.
items.cn: 英语经由法语借入，用于不合常理的故事。

items.en: The sense widened from untrue to merely astonishing.
items.cn: 词义从「不真」扩展到「仅仅令人吃惊」。

items.en: Spoken English added the sense of extremely good.
items.cn: 英语口语又添上「极好」的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cred- believe root; the near-meaning group holds words of surprise.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「相信」的 cred- 词根；近义组收表示「惊异」的词。

entries.definition: Able to be believed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可信的」，与本词只差一个 in-。

entries.definition: In a way that is hard to believe.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「难以置信地」。

entries.definition: Trust that allows buying now and paying later.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「信用、赊账」，同根。

entries.definition: Impossible or very hard to believe.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以置信的」，更口语。

entries.definition: So surprising that one is stunned.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「惊人的」，重在看后发懵。

entries.definition: Very surprising and impressive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人惊叹的」，偏褒义。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the believe root, the cred-credible pair and the everyday exclamation.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「相信」词根、cred/credible 对照与日常惊叹。

normal.en: Credit and creed both hold cred, believe, so incredible means simply not-credible.
normal.cn: credit 与 creed 里都含 cred「相信」，所以 incredible 就是「不可信的」。

normal.en: Take away in- and credible remains, which makes the pair the easiest negative in English.
normal.cn: 去掉 in- 剩下 credible，这一对是英语里最好记的否定搭配。

normal.en: When a story is incredible, the eyebrow moves before the mouth does.
normal.cn: 故事令人难以置信时，眉毛先于嘴巴做出反应。

normal.en: The same word praises dinner and prices, because both can pass belief.
normal.cn: 同一个词既夸晚饭也形容价格，因为两者都可能超出想象。

normal.en: An incredible amount is not a claim about truth but about the size of the pile.
normal.cn: an incredible amount 不是在说真假，而是在说那一堆有多大。

abstract.en: Belief is the most portable currency: it buys claims, goods and people alike.
abstract.cn: 相信是最通用的货币：它能买到说法、货物与人。

abstract.en: What is incredible is not always false, only unwitnessed.
abstract.cn: 难以置信的不一定假，只是尚未被亲眼看见。

abstract.en: Every wonder starts as a sentence the listener refuses to accept.
abstract.cn: 每一件奇事起初都是一句听者拒绝接受的话。

examples.en: They made an incredible amount of noise.
examples.cn: 他们弄出了惊人的动静。

examples.en: Her recovery was incredible to the doctors.
examples.cn: 她的康复让医生们难以置信。

examples.en: What an incredible meal that was!
examples.cn: 那顿饭真是好极了！

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因克瑞德」——因一张信用卡被克扣，账单令人难以置信。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ credere（相信）→ incredibilis；同根词有 credible、credit、credibility、creed、credential。

sensesIntro.en: Incredible begins as the simple denial of belief, then measures size, and finally becomes a spoken word of praise.
sensesIntro.cn: incredible 起初只是对「相信」的简单否定，后来用来衡量大小，最后变成口语中的赞美。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyebrows jumping before the mouth can answer.
core.cn: 核心意象：嘴巴还没开口，眉毛先跳了起来。

branches.en: TRUTH LINE: the tale resists belief.
branches.cn: 真伪线：故事抗拒被相信。

branches.en: SIZE LINE: a quantity passes the limit of imagination.
branches.cn: 大小线：数量越过想象的边界。

branches.en: PRAISE LINE: everyday speech turns it into a compliment.
branches.cn: 赞美线：日常口语把它变成褒义词。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT LINE: conduct is judged too unlikely to accept.
branches.cn: 评判线：某种行为被判为难以接受。

branches.en: TONE LINE: one adjective can be a doubt or a compliment.
branches.cn: 语气线：同一个形容词既可是疑问也可是称赞。

intro.en: A negative prefix on a root meaning believe, with an adjective ending that makes it describable.
intro.cn: 一个否定前缀加意为「相信」的词根，再接形容词词尾，使之可用来形容事物。

latinIntro.en: Latin in-, not, plus credere, to believe, plus -ibilis, able to be, gave incredibilis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in-「不」加 credere「相信」加 -ibilis「可……的」，构成 incredibilis。

items.example: the root of credible and credit

definition_zh: 汽油；（作定语）汽油的；汽油蓝
definition_en: a light liquid fuel refined from petroleum and burned in the engines of cars, sold in Britain under this name rather than as gasoline
core_image: 油枪插进油箱，透明液体带着刺鼻气味灌进去，车子随即又能跑起来
scene: 冬天的清晨，加油站前排着长队，车窗上全是白雾。 By the time the tank was full of petrol, the driver's hands had gone numb.
sceneCN: 这里是「汽油」（第 1 个义项：机动车用的轻质燃料）；句意为加满汽油的时候，司机的手已经冻得发麻。图中可辨识物件：加油枪、结霜的车窗、跳动的油表。

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁词干构成的源词，指地下开采的原油，是 petrol 的上位概念
由 petrol 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「汽油的；含汽油的」
由希腊词根 petro-（岩石）与 chemical 复合，指石油化工产品

senses.title: Motor fuel refined from petroleum
senses.definition: a light, flammable liquid made from petroleum and used as fuel in the engines of cars and other vehicles
senses.definitionCN: 由石油炼制的轻质易燃液体，用作汽车等内燃机的燃料
senses.example: The car ran out of petrol halfway up the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 车在上坡途中没油了。
senses.why: British drivers name the fluid itself, and the word began as a shortening of petroleum spirit, the thin fraction that boils off crude oil first and burns most easily in an engine.
senses.whyCN: 英国人说这个词时指的是那种液体本身；它最初是 petroleum spirit（石油精）的缩略，也就是原油蒸馏时最先沸腾、在发动机里最容易燃烧的轻馏分，所以词义天然落在「车用轻质燃料」上。

senses.title: Used before a noun for anything running on this fuel
senses.definition: placed before another noun to describe an engine, vehicle or place that uses or supplies this fuel
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，说明某发动机、车辆或场所使用或供应这种燃料
senses.example: He pulled into a petrol station just before midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜前他把车开进了一个加油站。
senses.why: Because everyday British speech has no verb of its own for refuelling, the fuel word is simply set in front of nouns such as engine, tank and station, where it labels whatever runs on it.
senses.whyCN: 日常英式表达里没有专门表示「加油」的动词形式，于是这个燃料词被直接放在 engine、tank、station 这类名词前面，给一切靠它运转的东西贴标签，定语用法就是这样固定下来的。

senses.title: A deep blue-green shade
senses.definition: a dark blue-green colour named after the rainbow film that fuel leaves on water
senses.definitionCN: 一种深蓝绿色调，得名于燃料在水面留下的彩虹色油膜
senses.example: The kitchen wall was painted petrol blue.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房的墙刷成了汽油蓝。
senses.why: Thin oil on a wet road shows a shifting blue-green sheen, and decorators borrowed the fuel's name for that exact shade, so the colour sense is the same liquid seen in a different light.
senses.whyCN: 湿路面上的一层薄油会泛出流动的蓝绿色光泽，室内设计师便借燃料之名来称呼这种具体的色调；所以颜色义项仍是同一种液体，只是换了一种光线去看。

intro.en: Petrol is a nineteenth-century shortening of petroleum spirit, and its family goes back through French to a medieval Latin name meaning rock oil.
intro.cn: petrol 是十九世纪对 petroleum spirit（石油精）的缩略，其词族经法语上溯到中世纪拉丁语中意为「岩石油」的名称。

items.en: Greek petra meant rock or stone, and it supplied the first half of the later name for oil that seeps out of stone.
items.cn: 希腊语 petra 意为岩石、石头，为后来「从石头里渗出的油」这一名称提供了前半部分。

items.en: Latin oleum meant oil, and the two elements were later joined to describe mineral oil rather than plant oil.
items.cn: 拉丁语 oleum 意为油；后来两个成分被拼在一起，用来指矿物油而不是植物油。

items.en: Medieval Latin petroleum, literally rock oil, named the oily substance that seeped from rock and was once sold as medicine.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 petroleum 字面即「岩石油」，指从岩石中渗出的油状物，曾作为药物出售。

items.en: French pétrole named the refined oil, while English pharmacists spoke of petroleum spirit for the light, volatile part of it.
items.cn: 法语 pétrole 指炼出的油，英语药剂师则用 petroleum spirit 称呼其中轻而易挥发的那一部分。

items.en: English cut petroleum spirit down to petrol in the late nineteenth century, and the short form became the everyday British word for motor fuel.
items.cn: 十九世纪后期英语把 petroleum spirit 截短为 petrol，这个短形式后来成为英式英语里指车用燃料的日常词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same rock-and-oil stem; the near-meaning group gathers other fuels sold at the same pump.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「岩石加油」词干上的词；近义组收在同一个加油机上出售的其他燃料。

entries.definition: The crude oil from which petrol is refined; the longer source word.
entries.definitionCN: 汽油由它炼制而来的原油，也是 petrol 的长形式源词。

entries.definition: A chemical obtained from petroleum or natural gas.
entries.definitionCN: 从石油或天然气中提取的化学品。

entries.definition: The scientific study of rocks, built on the same Greek word for rock.
entries.definitionCN: 研究岩石的科学，建立在同一个表示「岩石」的希腊词上。

entries.definition: Containing or yielding petroleum, as certain rock layers do.
entries.definitionCN: 含石油或产石油的，如某些岩层。

entries.definition: The American word for the same motor fuel.
entries.definitionCN: 美式英语里指同一种车用燃料的词。

entries.definition: A heavier fuel burned in a different kind of engine.
entries.definitionCN: 一种更重的燃料，用于另一种发动机。

entries.definition: Any material burned or consumed to produce heat or power.
entries.definitionCN: 任何燃烧或消耗以产生热或动力的材料。

entries.definition: A thin oil used in lamps and jet engines, lighter than diesel.
entries.definitionCN: 用于灯和喷气发动机的轻质油，比柴油更轻。

normalIntro.en: Petrol is a clipped piece of a much older compound, so its family keeps returning to rock, oil and the lightest part of both.
normalIntro.cn: petrol 是从一个古老得多的复合词里截下来的，所以它的同族词总是回到岩石、油以及两者中最轻的那一部分。

normal.en: Petrol is a clipped form of petroleum spirit, so the word still carries the idea of the lightest part of crude oil.
normal.cn: petrol 是 petroleum spirit 的截短形式，所以这个词始终带着「原油中最轻那部分」的意思。

normal.en: The same stem appears in petroleum, petrochemical and petrology, all tied to rock and the oil drawn from it.
normal.cn: 同一词干出现在 petroleum、petrochemical、petrology 里，都与岩石以及从岩石中取得的油有关。

normal.en: British petrol and American gasoline name the same pump fuel, so a naming habit rather than a chemical difference separates them.
normal.cn: 英式 petrol 与美式 gasoline 指同一种加油站的燃料，分开它们的只是命名习惯，而不是化学成分。

normal.en: Petrol station, petrol tank and petrol engine show the word behaving like a fixed label in front of nouns.
normal.cn: petrol station、petrol tank、petrol engine 表明这个词常像固定标签一样放在名词前。

normal.en: Petrol blue is not a joke: the word for the fuel also names the blue-green film it leaves on water.
normal.cn: petrol blue 不是玩笑：这个燃料词也用来命名它在水面留下的蓝绿色油膜。

abstract.en: Picture the clear liquid sliding down the filler neck: the word names the moment a car becomes able to move again.
abstract.cn: 想象透明液体顺着加油口流下去：这个词命名的正是汽车重新能跑起来的那一刻。

abstract.en: A fuel thin enough to explode in a cylinder is also thin enough to shimmer on a puddle, which is why one word covers both.
abstract.cn: 薄到能在气缸里爆燃的燃料，也薄到能在水洼上泛光，于是一个词同时覆盖了这两件事。

abstract.en: Every litre of petrol is ancient sunlight stored underground and released in a few minutes of driving.
abstract.cn: 每一升汽油都是储存在地下的远古阳光，在几分钟的驾驶里被释放出来。

examples.en: The car ran out of petrol halfway up the hill.
examples.cn: 车在上坡途中没油了。

examples.en: Petrol prices rose again before the holiday.
examples.cn: 假期前汽油价格又涨了。

examples.en: He pulled into a petrol station just before midnight.
examples.cn: 午夜前他把车开进了一个加油站。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼漏」——油箱一颠，油泼出来又漏下去；petrol 是汽油。

root: 拉丁语 petra（岩石，源自希腊语）加 oleum（油）构成中世纪拉丁语 petroleum，经法语进入英语；十九世纪截短为 petrol，专指原油炼出的轻质车用燃料。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the light fuel burned in a car engine; from it come the attributive label for petrol-driven things and the colour named after an oil film.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是汽车发动机里燃烧的轻质燃料；由此分出去定语用法（汽油驱动的）与以油膜命名的颜色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nozzle clicking shut as clear fuel rises inside the tank.
core.cn: 核心意象：透明燃料在油箱里升高，加油枪咔哒一声跳停。

branches.en: a pump nozzle clicking off as the tank fills
branches.cn: 加油枪在油箱加满时咔哒一声跳停

branches.en: a needle on the dashboard dropping toward empty
branches.cn: 仪表盘上的指针滑向空位

branches.en: a station lit up at midnight beside a dark road
branches.cn: 深夜公路旁亮着灯的加油站

branches.en: a blue-green sheen spreading over a rain puddle
branches.cn: 蓝绿色光泽在雨后的水洼上散开

branches.en: the same thin liquid, once burned and once reflected
branches.cn: 同一种轻质液体，一面被烧掉，一面被映照

intro.en: The word is a compound of a Greek rock word and a Latin oil word, later clipped and pressed into service as the British name for motor fuel.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语的「岩石」与拉丁语的「油」复合而成，后来被截短，用作英式英语里车用燃料的名称。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: oil or alcohol in chemical names
items.meaningCN: 化学名称中表示油或醇的后缀
出售燃料的地方；加油站

definition_zh: 推迟；耽搁；延迟
definition_en: to make something happen later than planned, or the time lost by waiting
core_image: 站台上的人群一起抬头看晚点的牌子
scene: 大雪压住了铁轨，清晨的列车一班接一班停在站外。 Heavy snow delayed the morning trains.
sceneCN: 这里 delay 指「耽搁」（第 1 个义项：使事情比计划更晚发生）；句意是大雪让早班列车晚点。

derivatives.zh: 被延误的
拖延的
未受延误的
拖延者

senses.title: Make it happen later
senses.definition: to arrange for something to take place at a later time
senses.definitionCN: 把某事安排到更晚的时间进行
senses.example: They delayed the meeting until Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把会议推迟到星期五。
senses.why: A thing put off is a thing still waiting on the shelf.
senses.whyCN: 被推迟的事，就是还搁在架子上等着的。

senses.title: Hold someone up on the way
senses.definition: to make a person or vehicle late by slowing them down
senses.definitionCN: 因拖慢速度而使人或车辆迟到
senses.example: Heavy snow delayed the morning trains.
senses.exampleCN: 大雪让早班列车晚点。
senses.why: One slow point on a road makes every traveller late.
senses.whyCN: 路上一个慢下来的地方，就让所有赶路的人迟到。

senses.title: The time lost in waiting
senses.definition: the period of waiting caused by something being late
senses.definitionCN: 因某事迟到而产生的等待时间
senses.example: There was a delay of two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 延误了两个小时。
senses.why: Waiting is the shape that lost time takes in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 等待，就是失去的时间在心里留下的形状。

intro.en: Delay comes from Old French delaier, to put off, built on Latin laxare, to loosen.
intro.cn: delay 来自古法语 delaier（往后放），底层是拉丁语 laxare（放松、松开）。

items.en: Laxare meant to loosen a hold or a rope.
items.cn: laxare 意为把抓住的手或绳子松开。

items.en: Delaier joined de- with laier, to leave something for later.
items.cn: delaier 由 de- 与 laier 合成，意为留到以后再说。

items.en: English used delay for both putting off and being held up.
items.cn: 英语用它既指主动推迟，也指被动耽搁。

items.en: The noun delay settled into talk of journeys and courts.
items.cn: 名词用法在旅途与法庭的说法里安定下来。

items.en: Trains, flights and replies are all said to be delayed.
items.cn: 如今列车、航班和回复都可以说被延误。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ay ending, and the meaning group names three ways of making something wait.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -ay 这个尾巴，近义组则是三种让人或事等一等的方式。

entries.definition: to pass a message or signal on
entries.definitionCN: 转达消息或转播信号

entries.definition: to be slowly destroyed by natural causes
entries.definitionCN: 因自然作用慢慢腐坏

entries.definition: to make a fear or worry less strong
entries.definitionCN: 减轻恐惧或忧虑

entries.definition: to move an event to a later date
entries.definitionCN: 把活动改到更晚的日期

entries.definition: to decide to do something later
entries.definitionCN: 决定以后再去做

entries.definition: to stop something from moving on time
entries.definitionCN: 使某事不能按时进行

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a crowd looking up at a board and end with two hours that simply vanished.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一群人抬头看牌子开始，落到凭空消失的两个小时。

normal.en: A train is late once, but the waiting is repeated by everyone.
normal.cn: 列车只晚一次，等待却被每个人各经历一遍。

normal.en: Delay is not a stop; the wheels are still turning, only slower.
normal.cn: 耽搁不是停下，轮子还在转，只是慢了。

normal.en: The meeting moved by two days costs two days of guessing.
normal.cn: 会议挪两天，就多出两天猜测。

normal.en: To delay a reply is to say nothing in a loud way.
normal.cn: 拖着不回，就是用很响的方式什么也不说。

normal.en: Relay passes a message on; delay keeps it back.
normal.cn: relay 把消息传下去，delay 把消息留住。

abstract.en: Picture a clock with one hand moving slower than the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，一根针走得比另一根慢。

abstract.en: Picture a queue that does not move but grows.
abstract.cn: 想象一支不往前挪、却越来越长的队伍。

abstract.en: Picture a letter left in a drawer for a week.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信在抽屉里躺了一星期。

examples.en: Heavy snow delayed the morning trains.
examples.cn: 大雪让早班列车晚点。

examples.en: They delayed the meeting until Friday.
examples.cn: 他们把会议推迟到星期五。

examples.en: There was a delay of two hours.
examples.cn: 延误了两个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 delay 记成「地雷」：路上踩到地雷，队伍就走不动，只好延误。

root: 来自古法语 delaier（留到以后），其底层是拉丁语 laxare（松开），本义是把抓着的事放开、让它往后滑。它先指主动推迟，后来也指被动耽搁，如今连列车、航班与回复晚到都用它。

sensesIntro.en: From a plan moved forward on the calendar, to a train held in the snow, to the empty hours that remain.
sensesIntro.cn: 从日历上往后挪的计划，到被雪挡住的列车，再到剩下那几个空掉的小时。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a station board where one line turns late.
core.cn: 核心意象：车站牌上有一行变成了晚点。

branches.en: The first sense moves the agreed time further on.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把商定的时间往后挪。

branches.en: The second sense is being slowed on the way.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是在路上被拖慢。

branches.en: The third sense is the waiting that results.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是由此产生的等待。

branches.en: A choice and an accident produce the same lateness.
branches.cn: 主动的选择与被动的意外，造成同一种晚。

branches.en: The train and the empty hour are one event seen twice.
branches.cn: 晚点的列车与空掉的一小时，是同一件事的两面。

intro.en: Delay forms a few adjectives and nouns, all about lateness and waiting.
intro.cn: delay 能派生出几个形容词与名词，全都与晚点和等待有关。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is laxare, to loosen, with de- giving the sense of away.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 laxare（松开），前缀 de- 带来「离开」的意味。

items.meaning: to put off, or the wait
items.example: The delay was caused by fog.
The delayed train arrived at noon.
A delaying tactic bought them a day.
items.exampleCN: 拖延的办法为他们争到一天。

items.example: He was the delayer of every plan.
items.exampleCN: 每个计划都是他拖下来的。

items.example: A long delay tested our patience.
items.exampleCN: 漫长的延误考验了我们的耐性。

items.meaning: a gap between act and result
items.example: There is a short time delay in the signal.

definition_zh: 巨大的；庞大的；极大的
definition_en: extremely large in size, amount, or degree
core_image: 一头鲸从船边浮起，船在它旁边像一片叶子
scene: 博物馆大厅中央立着一具恐龙骨架，参观者站在下面显得很小。 The skeleton was enormous, filling the whole hall.
sceneCN: 这里 enormous 是「巨大的」（第 1 个义项：尺寸极大）；句意：这具骨架极其巨大，占满了整个大厅。

derivatives.zh: 极大地；非常
巨大；严重性
巨大

senses.title: Extremely large in size
senses.definition: much bigger than usual or expected
senses.definitionCN: 比通常或预期大得多
senses.example: An enormous tree stood in the middle of the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 花园中央立着一棵巨大的树。
senses.why: The Latin source means outside the rule, and something outside normal measure is first of all huge.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「超出常规」，而超出常规尺度的东西首先就是巨大的。

senses.title: Extremely great in degree
senses.definition: very great in amount, power, or importance
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、力量或重要性上极大
senses.example: The project required an enormous amount of work.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目需要极大的工作量。
senses.why: The same sense of exceeding normal limits applies to abstract quantities such as effort and pressure.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「超出正常限度」也适用于努力、压力等抽象数量。

senses.title: Outrageous or monstrous
senses.definition: shockingly bad or wicked, an older literary sense
senses.definitionCN: 令人震惊地坏或邪恶，较古老的文学义项
senses.example: The poem describes an enormous crime against the innocent.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗描述了一桩针对无辜者的骇人罪行。
senses.why: Something outside the rule of right conduct was originally called enormous before the word shifted to size.
senses.whyCN: 超出正当行为之「常规」的事，原本就被称作 enormous，后来词义才转向尺寸。

intro.en: Enormous comes from Latin enormis, outside the rule, from e-, out of, and norma, a rule or square.
intro.cn: enormous 来自拉丁语 enormis（超出常规），由 e-（出于）与 norma（规则、曲尺）构成。

items.en: Norma means a carpenter's square and then any rule or standard.
items.cn: norma 指木匠的曲尺，后来泛指规则或标准。

items.en: Enormis means out of rule, irregular, and therefore monstrous or shocking.
items.cn: enormis 意为不合规则的、异常的，因此有「骇人」之意。

items.en: Old French enorme keeps the sense of something shocking and excessive.
items.cn: 古法语 enorme 保留「骇人、过度」的意思。

items.en: Middle English enormous describes both wicked acts and great size.
items.cn: 中古英语 enormous 既描述邪恶行为，也描述巨大尺寸。

items.en: The size sense becomes dominant in ordinary usage.
items.cn: 到 18 世纪，尺寸义在日常用法中占据主导。

items.en: Modern English uses enormous mainly for very great size or amount.
items.cn: 现代英语主要用 enormous 表示极大的尺寸或数量。

note.en: Enormous belongs to the norm family, and it sits near adjectives for very great size.
note.cn: enormous 属于「常规」词族，与表示极大尺寸的形容词相邻。

entries.definition: very much
entries.definitionCN: 极大地

entries.definition: the great size or seriousness of something
entries.definitionCN: 巨大；严重性

entries.definition: a standard or usual level
entries.definitionCN: 标准；常规

entries.definition: very large
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的

entries.definition: extremely large
entries.definitionCN: 广大的；巨大的

normalIntro.en: Enormous contains norm, so the memory hook is something so big that it is outside the normal measure.
normalIntro.cn: enormous 含有 norm，记忆钩子是「大到超出了正常尺度」。

normal.en: E- means out of, and norm means rule: outside the rule, therefore huge.
normal.cn: e- 表示出于，norm 表示规则：超出规则，所以巨大。

normal.en: Enormous amount is the most common abstract collocation.
normal.cn: enormous amount 是最常见的抽象搭配。

normal.en: The ending -ly gives enormously, meaning very much.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 构成 enormously，意为「极大地」。

normal.en: Compare huge and enormous: enormous often adds a sense of excess.
normal.cn: 对比 huge 与 enormous：enormous 常多一层「过度」的意味。

normal.en: The noun enormity can mean great seriousness as well as great size.
normal.cn: 名词 enormity 既可指巨大，也可指严重性。

abstract.en: Picture a whale surfacing beside a small boat.

abstract.en: Imagine standing under a dinosaur skeleton that fills a hall.

root: 拉丁语 e-（出于）+ norma（规则、曲尺）→ enormis（不合常规的、骇人的）→ 古法语 enorme → 中古英语 enormous，后以「巨大」为主要义项。

sensesIntro.en: Being outside the rule first described monstrous things, then huge ones, and the size sense now reaches both physical and abstract quantities.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something so large that it exceeds every normal measure.

branches.en: Physical size beyond expectation is the everyday sense.

branches.en: Abstract quantity beyond expectation extends the same excess.

branches.en: The old sense of monstrous or outrageous keeps the moral origin alive.
branches.cn: 「骇人、极恶」的旧义保留了这个词的道德起源。

branches.en: Big objects and big amounts both break the normal scale.
branches.cn: 巨大物体与巨大数量都突破正常尺度。

branches.en: Excess in degree can impress or horrify, depending on context.

definition_zh: 机械装置；机械结构；机制；机理；途径
definition_en: a set of connected moving parts, or an abstract arrangement of parts and processes that produces a particular result
core_image: 一排咬合的齿轮：每一枚只做一件事，连起来却推动整台机器
scene: 钟表匠掀开旧钟的后板，让里面的构件露出来。 The clockmaker lifted the back plate to show the mechanism of the old tower clock.
sceneCN: 这里 mechanism 是「机械结构、传动装置」（第 2 个义项：机器内部一起工作的部件与结构）；句意：钟表匠揭开后板，展示这座老塔钟的机械结构。场景要点：塔钟的黄铜后板、层层咬合的齿轮、钟表匠手里的放大镜；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 机械的；机械式的；呆板的
