senses.title: A set of moving parts
senses.definition: the parts of a device that move together to perform a particular action
senses.definitionCN: 装置中一起运动、完成特定动作的那些部件
senses.example: The locking mechanism jammed after years of use.
senses.exampleCN: 使用多年之后，锁具装置卡住了。
senses.why: Greek mēkhanē named a device, and the first English sense was the structure of a machine. The physical set of parts is the core image in its most concrete form.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 mēkhanē 指装置，英语最早的义项就是机器的结构。这一套实体部件，就是核心意象最具体的形态。

senses.title: The working structure inside a machine
senses.definition: the arrangement and interaction of a machine's parts, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 机器各部件作为整体时的排列与相互作用
senses.example: He explained the mechanism of the clock, gear by gear.
senses.exampleCN: 他一个齿轮一个齿轮地讲解这座钟的机械结构。
senses.why: Once the parts are seen together, attention shifts from the pieces to how they transmit motion. The word now names the logic inside the device.
senses.whyCN: 当部件被放在一起看，注意力就从零件本身转到它们如何传递运动。这个词于是命名装置内部的那套逻辑。

senses.title: An institutional mechanism
senses.definition: an established arrangement of rules, offices, and procedures that produces a result or handles a problem
senses.definitionCN: 由规则、机构和程序构成的既定安排，用来产生某种结果或处理某个问题
senses.example: The treaty set up a mechanism for settling border disputes.
senses.exampleCN: 这项条约建立了一套解决边界争端的机制。
senses.why: Institutions can be read as parts of a machine: each office turns one wheel, and the arrangement yields a decision. The physical picture is applied to procedure.
senses.whyCN: 制度可以被读成机器的零件：每个机构带动一只轮子，整套安排产出一个决定。物理画面被套用到了程序上。

senses.title: A biological mechanism
senses.definition: a set of bodily or cellular processes that produces a particular effect
senses.definitionCN: 身体或细胞层面的一组过程，产生特定效果
senses.example: The immune mechanism recognises the virus within hours.
senses.exampleCN: 免疫机制在数小时内就识别出这种病毒。
senses.why: A living body also has interlocking parts, though they are cells and signals rather than gears. The image survives because the result still depends on the parts acting in order.
senses.whyCN: 活的躯体也有相互咬合的部件，只不过它们是细胞与信号，而不是齿轮。意象仍然成立，因为结果依旧依赖各部件按次序行动。

senses.title: A psychological mechanism
senses.definition: a repeated mental process by which a person copes with feelings or situations
senses.definitionCN: 一个人用来应对情绪或处境的、反复出现的心理过程
senses.example: Mocking others can work as a defence mechanism.
senses.exampleCN: 嘲笑别人可以起到防御机制的作用。
senses.why: The mind is treated as an apparatus with parts: a feeling enters, a routine process turns it, and a behaviour comes out. The word lends machinery to psychology.
senses.whyCN: 心灵被当作一台有部件的装置：一种情绪进入，一套惯常过程把它转动，一种行为出来。这个词把机械感借给了心理学。

senses.title: A reaction mechanism in chemistry
senses.definition: the step-by-step sequence by which reactants become products, including intermediate states
senses.definitionCN: 反应物变成产物的逐步序列，包括中间状态
senses.example: The reaction mechanism involves two short-lived intermediates.
senses.exampleCN: 这个反应机理涉及两种寿命很短的中间体。
senses.why: A reaction is a process with stages, and each stage hands the matter on to the next like one gear driving another. The word names the hidden chain.
senses.whyCN: 反应是一个分阶段的过程，每一阶段把物质交给下一阶段，就像一只齿轮带动另一只。这个词命名的正是那条看不见的链条。

senses.title: The philosophical doctrine of mechanism
senses.definition: the view that natural events can be explained entirely by the motion of matter, without purpose or vital force
senses.definitionCN: 认为自然事件完全可以由物质运动来解释、无需目的或生命力 的观点
senses.example: Mechanism holds that life can be explained by matter and motion alone.
senses.exampleCN: 机械论认为生命仅凭物质与运动就能得到解释。
senses.why: Here the metaphor is taken all the way: the whole of nature is declared to be one machine. The word stops naming a device and starts naming a world view.
senses.whyCN: 这里把比喻推到了底：整个自然被宣告为一台机器。这个词不再命名某个装置，而开始命名一种世界观。

senses.title: A means or channel for doing something
senses.definition: a method, channel, or route through which something can be done
senses.definitionCN: 完成某事所经由的方法、渠道或途径
senses.example: The committee has no mechanism for enforcing its decisions.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会没有执行其决定的机制。
senses.why: If a result is produced by parts working in order, then any such arrangement is a way to get the result. The concrete device thins into 'means'.
senses.whyCN: 如果结果由部件按次序工作产生，那么任何这样的安排都是取得结果的一条路。具体装置于是淡化成“手段”。

intro.en: Mechanism came into English in the 1660s from Modern Latin mechanismus, built on Greek mēkhanē 'machine, device'. The Greek-to-Latin route is clear; the deeper Indo-European link is disputed.
intro.cn: mechanism 于 17 世纪 60 年代由现代拉丁语 mechanismus 进入英语，后者建立在希腊语 mēkhanē“机械、装置”之上。希腊语到拉丁语的路径清楚；更深的印欧语关联存在争议。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'the structure of a machine, engine, or other contrivance for controlling or utilizing natural forces'. The source is Modern Latin mechanismus.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 17 世纪 60 年代，意为“机器、引擎或其他用来控制或利用自然力的装置的结构”。来源是现代拉丁语 mechanismus。

items.en: The broader sense 'a mechanical contrivance or agency of any kind' is recorded. From here the word begins to detach from literal hardware and to name any working arrangement.
items.cn: 较宽的义项“任何种类的机械装置或作用机构”有记录。自此这个词开始脱离字面上的硬件，用来命名任何一套运作安排。

items.en: Mechanismus was formed from Greek mēkhanē plus the Latin noun suffix -ismus. It is a scholarly coinage, not an inherited Latin word.
items.cn: mechanismus 由希腊语 mēkhanē 加拉丁名词后缀 -ismus 构成。它是学术性的新造词，不是继承下来的拉丁词。

items.en: Greek mēkhanē, with the Doric variant makhana, meant 'device, tool, machine', and also 'contrivance, cunning'. It is the source of machine and mechanic as well as mechanism.
items.cn: 希腊语 mēkhanē（多里斯方言作 makhana）意为“装置、工具、机械”，也有“计谋、机巧”的意思。它既是 machine、mechanic 的来源，也是 mechanism 的来源。

items.en: Watkins derived mēkhanē from PIE *magh- 'to be able, have power', the root behind may, might and magic. Beekes rejects this on formal grounds and treats the Greek word as Pre-Greek, so the deepest root is disputed and best marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 沃特金斯把 mēkhanē 追溯到原始印欧语 *magh-“能够、有力量”，该词根也是 may、might、magic 的来源。比克斯从形式证据上反对这一联系，认为这个希腊词属于前希腊语底层，因此最深词源有争议，宜标为来源不确定。

items.en: Mechanic, mechanical, mechanics, mechanize and mechanistic all belong to the same family. Mechanism keeps two lives: a concrete device, and an abstract system of parts and processes.
items.cn: mechanic、mechanical、mechanics、mechanize、mechanistic 都属于同一词族。mechanism 保有两条命：一个是具体装置，一个是由部件与过程构成的抽象系统。

note.en: The first group separates the whole machine, the mass noun, the person and the adjective. The second group compares mechanism with apparatus, device, process and system.
note.cn: 第一组区分整台机器、集合名词、人和形容词；第二组把 mechanism 与 apparatus、device、process、system 作比较。

entries.definition: a complete device with moving parts that does a job. Mechanism is the arrangement inside such a device, or the abstract version of that arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 一台有活动部件、能完成某项工作的完整装置。mechanism 是这种装置内部的排列，或这种排列的抽象版本。

entries.definition: machines as a group, or the moving parts of a machine taken as a mass. It is uncountable, while a mechanism is one countable arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 机器的总称，或作为整体看的一台机器的活动部件。它不可数，而 mechanism 是一套可数的排列。

entries.definition: a person who repairs or operates machines. It names a worker, not the working arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 修理或操作机器的人。它命名的是工人，而不是运作的结构。

entries.definition: explaining things as if they were produced by machinery. It describes a view or style, not a device.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物当作由机械产生来解释的。它描述一种观点或风格，而不是一件装置。

entries.definition: a set of equipment assembled for a particular purpose, often scientific. It names the whole set-up, while mechanism stresses how the parts work together.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定目的组装的一套设备，常用于科学场景。它命名整套装备，而 mechanism 强调部件如何一起运作。

entries.definition: an object invented to do a particular job. A device is what it is; a mechanism is how it works.
entries.definitionCN: 为完成特定工作而发明的物件。device 说的是“它是什么”，mechanism 说的是“它怎样运作”。

entries.definition: a series of actions that leads to a result. It gives the order of stages; mechanism adds the interlocking parts that carry the stages out.
entries.definitionCN: 导向结果的一系列行动。它给出阶段的顺序；mechanism 则补上执行这些阶段的咬合部件。

entries.definition: an organized set of parts or rules. It is broader than mechanism: a system may be social or biological, and it need not have a visible causal chain.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的部件或规则集合。它比 mechanism 更宽：系统可以是社会的或生物的，也不必有可见的因果链。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Greek mēkhanē 'device', machine and mechanic, and the modern family mechanical / mechanics / mechanize.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：希腊语 mēkhanē“装置”，machine 与 mechanic，以及现代词族 mechanical／mechanics／mechanize。

normal.en: Greek mēkhanē meant 'device, tool, machine'. Mechanism is the Latin-built noun for the way such a device is put together.
normal.cn: 希腊语 mēkhanē 意为“装置、工具、机械”。mechanism 是拉丁语构造的名词，指这种装置被组装起来的方式。

normal.en: Machine, mechanic and mechanism share one Greek source. The machine is the whole object, the mechanic is the person, and the mechanism is the working arrangement.
normal.cn: machine、mechanic、mechanism 共享同一个希腊来源。机器是整体物件，技师是人，机制则是运作的排列。

normal.en: Mechanical is the adjective, mechanics is the science of forces and motion, and mechanize is to replace hands with machinery.
normal.cn: mechanical 是形容词，mechanics 是研究力与运动的科学，mechanize 则是用机械取代人手。

normal.en: A defence mechanism, a reaction mechanism and a market mechanism all keep the same picture: parts in contact, each turning the next.
normal.cn: 防御机制、反应机理与市场机制都保留同一幅画面：部件相互接触，每一枚带动下一枚。

normal.en: Mechanistic is the adjective for a view that treats everything as machinery; it is a judgement about an explanation, not a description of a device.
normal.cn: mechanistic 是形容词，指把一切当作机械的看法；它是对某种解释的评判，而不是对装置的描述。

abstract.en: Picture a row of gears. No single gear can do the job alone; the result appears only when each one passes motion to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一排齿轮。没有任何一只齿轮能独自完成工作；只有当每一只把运动传给下一只，结果才出现。

abstract.en: A mechanism is a way of hiding the work: you see a handle turn, but the useful result happens inside the box.
abstract.cn: 机制是一种把劳动藏起来的方式：你看见手柄在转，真正有用的结果却发生在盒子内部。

abstract.en: The same word serves a lock, an immune system and a treaty because all three produce a result through parts that depend on one another.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能用于一把锁、一套免疫系统和一项条约，因为这三者都通过彼此依赖的部件产出一个结果。

examples.en: The engineer traced the fault to a worn cam in the valve mechanism.
examples.cn: 工程师把故障追查到阀门装置里一只磨损的凸轮。

examples.en: Scientists still argue about the exact mechanism by which the drug works.
examples.cn: 科学家仍在争论这种药起效的确切机理。

examples.en: The two countries agreed on a mechanism for sharing river water.
examples.cn: 两国就共享河水的一套机制达成了一致。

dict_mnemonic.text: “麦克你怎”——麦克，你怎把这一排齿轮装进盒子？→ mechanism 机械装置、机制

root: 源自希腊语 mēkhanē“机械、装置”，经现代拉丁语 mechanismus 进入英语，核心是“一组咬合部件按次序把运动传下去”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of mechanism, all from one picture: interlocking parts, each doing one small job, together producing a result — whether the parts are gears, cells, institutions, or steps in a reaction.
sensesIntro.cn: mechanism 的八个义项都来自同一幅画面：相互咬合的部件，每个只做一件小事，合起来产出一个结果——无论这些部件是齿轮、细胞、机构，还是反应中的步骤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of interlocking gears, each passing motion to the next.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排咬合的齿轮，每一只把运动传给下一只。

branches.en: HARDWARE: a lock or a clock is a set of parts, and the mechanism is both the parts and the way they move together.
branches.cn: 硬件：一把锁或一座钟是一套部件，mechanism 既是这些部件，也是它们一起运动的方式。

branches.en: ARRANGEMENTS AND MEANS: institutions and procedures can be arranged like parts, and any such arrangement is a way to get a result.
branches.cn: 安排与手段：机构与程序可以像部件一样被安排，而任何这样的安排都是取得结果的一条路。

branches.en: LIFE AND MIND: immune responses and defence routines are hidden processes whose parts still depend on one another.
branches.cn: 生命与心灵：免疫反应与防御套路都是隐藏的过程，其部件同样彼此依赖。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY: a reaction mechanism is the step-by-step chain that turns reactants into products.
branches.cn: 化学：反应机理是把反应物变成产物的逐步链条。

branches.en: PHILOSOPHY: mechanism turns the metaphor into a world view, declaring all of nature to be one machine.
branches.cn: 哲学：机械论把比喻提升为世界观，宣告整个自然就是一台机器。

intro.en: Mechanism is Greek mēkhanē fitted with a Latin noun suffix. English then adds -ical, -ics, -ize and -ation, and the same Greek root also gives machine and machinery.
intro.cn: mechanism 是希腊语 mēkhanē 装上拉丁名词后缀构成的。英语随后加上 -ical、-ics、-ize、-ation，同一个希腊词根还给出 machine 与 machinery。

latinIntro.en: Modern Latin mechanismus is a scholarly compound of Greek mēkhanē and Latin -ismus. Latin also borrowed the Greek noun as machina, which is the direct source of English machine and machinery.
latinIntro.cn: 现代拉丁语 mechanismus 是希腊语 mēkhanē 与拉丁后缀 -ismus 的学术复合词。拉丁语还把希腊名词借作 machina，这正是英语 machine 与 machinery 的直接来源。

items.meaning: a working arrangement of parts; a system that produces a result
items.meaningCN: 部件的运作排列；产生结果的机制（mēkhanē 装置 + -ismus 名词后缀）
items.example: The clock's mechanism needs cleaning every year.
items.exampleCN: 这座钟的机械结构每年都要清洗。

items.example: The body uses several mechanisms to control heat.
items.exampleCN: 身体用好几套机制来控制体温。

items.meaning: explaining things as if by machinery
items.meaningCN: 机械论的；机械式解释的（-istic 构成形容词）
items.example: A mechanistic view leaves no room for purpose.
items.exampleCN: 机械论的观点不给目的留下空间。

items.meaning: to replace manual work with machinery
items.meaningCN: 使机械化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The farm mechanized harvesting in the 1950s.
items.exampleCN: 这个农场在 20 世纪 50 年代实现了收割机械化。

items.meaningCN: 机械化（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Mechanization cut the need for seasonal labour.
items.exampleCN: 机械化减少了对季节性劳动力的需求。

items.meaning: working by machinery; done without thought
items.meaningCN: 机械的；机械式的；呆板的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The lift stopped because of a mechanical fault.
items.exampleCN: 电梯因机械故障停了下来。

items.meaning: by means of machinery; without thought
items.meaningCN: 机械地；用机械方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 她机械地回答，根本没在听。

items.meaning: the science of forces and motion; the way something works
items.meaningCN: 力学；机械学；运作方式（-ics 表示学科）
items.example: The mechanics of the trade are taught in the first term.
items.exampleCN: 这门行业的具体运作方式在第一学期教授。

items.meaningCN: 机械师；修理工（拉丁语 mechanicus，源自希腊语）
items.example: The mechanic replaced the worn bearing.
items.exampleCN: 修理工更换了磨损的轴承。

items.meaning: a device with moving parts that does work
items.meaningCN: 机器（拉丁语 machina，源自希腊语 mēkhanē）
items.example: The machine prints two thousand labels an hour.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器每小时印两千张标签。

items.meaning: machines as a group; the working parts of a machine
items.meaningCN: 机器总称；机器的运转部件（-ery 构成集合名词）
items.example: The factory replaced its old machinery.

items.meaning: a prefix meaning mechanical or machine-related
items.meaningCN: 表示“机械的、与机械有关的”构词成分
items.example: A mechanoreceptor responds to touch or pressure.
items.exampleCN: 机械感受器对触碰或压力作出反应。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 机器的结构（现代拉丁语新造词）

latinEntries.meaning: mechanical; a person skilled in machines

definition_zh: 高效的；能干的；有产生力的
definition_en: working well with little waste, organized and capable, or having the power to produce an effect
core_image: 一条流水线，零件进来，成品出去，地上没有剩料
scene: 换上新电机后，同样的活只用一半时间就干完了。 The new motor is twice as efficient as the old one.
sceneCN: 这里 efficient 是「高效的」（第 1 个义项：以较少的投入完成同样的工作）；句意是新电机比旧电机效率高一倍。

pos.zh: 形容词：高效的；能干的；有产生力的

senses.title: Working without waste
senses.definition: working well and completely, with little waste of time, energy or materials
senses.definitionCN: 做事又好又完整，很少浪费时间、精力或材料
senses.example: The new motor is twice as efficient as the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 新电机比旧电机效率高一倍。
senses.why: Efficient is the Latin efficiens, doing or accomplishing: a thing that gets the work done without spending more than it must.
senses.whyCN: efficient 是拉丁语 efficiens，意为「正在做成的」：把活干成，却不比必须的多花一分。

senses.title: Organized and capable
senses.definition: of a person, organized and able to do a job well and quickly
senses.definitionCN: 指人时，有条理、能把事情做好做快
senses.example: She is an efficient manager who never wastes a meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个能干的经理，从不开没有结果的会。
senses.why: A person who finishes work without waste shows the same power to accomplish, so the adjective moves from machines to people.
senses.whyCN: 不浪费却把活完成的人，显露的是同一种「做成」的力量，于是这个形容词从机器移到了人身上。

senses.title: Having the power to produce an effect
senses.definition: having the power to bring about a result, as in the technical phrase efficient cause
senses.definitionCN: 具有产生结果的力量，用于「动力因」这一术语
senses.example: In philosophy, an efficient cause is what brings something about.
senses.exampleCN: 在哲学里，动力因就是使某物产生的东西。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply producing: an efficient cause is the doer that makes the effect exist.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是「产生」：动力因是让结果存在起来的那个施行者。

intro.en: Efficient comes from Latin efficiens, the present participle of efficere, to accomplish, and reached English through French.
intro.cn: efficient 来自拉丁语 efficiens，即 efficere（完成）的现在分词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Facere meant to do or make and supplied the base of the verb.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，提供这个动词的词基。

items.en: Ex- out plus facere formed efficere, to work out or accomplish.
items.cn: 表示「出」的 ex- 加 facere 构成 efficere，意为「做出、完成」。

items.en: The participle efficiens described something as accomplishing or producing.
items.cn: 分词 efficiens 描述某物正在完成或正在产生。

items.en: French passed the adjective on with the sense of producing a result.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词传下来，意思是「能产生结果的」。

items.en: Industry added the everyday sense of working without waste of time or fuel.
items.cn: 工业又加入了日常义：不浪费时间或燃料地把活干好。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the efficiency family; the near-meaning group separates effective, productive and economical.
note.cn: 形近组收 efficiency 词族；近义组区分 effective、productive 与 economical。

entries.definition: The quality of working without waste, or the output-to-input ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「效率」，即不浪费的品质或产出投入之比。

entries.definition: In a manner that wastes little time or energy.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「高效地」，很少浪费时间或精力。

entries.definition: The power to reach the intended result, with no claim about waste.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「有效性」，只管结果达没达到，不管浪不浪费。

entries.definition: Producing the result wanted; it asks whether the aim is reached, not what it cost.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有效的」，只问目标是否达到，不问成本。

entries.definition: Producing a good amount of work or goods; it stresses output.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多产的」，强调产出量。

entries.definition: Saving money or resources; it stresses the cost spared.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「节约的」，强调省下的花费。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a line that leaves no scrap on the floor, then move to a tidy manager and to a cause that makes things happen.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一条地上没有剩料的流水线出发，再走到干练的经理与「让事情发生」的原因。

normal.en: Efficient means the same work with less fuel, less time and less scrap.
normal.cn: efficient 就是用更少的燃料、时间和废料完成同样的活。

normal.en: An efficient manager ends the meeting when the decision is made.
normal.cn: 能干的经理在决定做出时就结束会议。

normal.en: Efficient and effective are cousins: one saves, the other arrives.
normal.cn: efficient 与 effective 是表亲：一个讲省，一个讲结果到了。

normal.en: The old philosophical sense is plain: efficient cause means the doer.
normal.cn: 古老的哲学义很直白：efficient cause 就是那个施行者。

normal.en: Efficiency is the noun, efficiently the adverb, inefficient the opposite.

abstract.en: Look at the floor: nothing usable is left lying there.
abstract.cn: 再看地面：没有还能用的东西被丢在那里。

abstract.en: Efficient is that picture of full output and empty waste.
abstract.cn: efficient 就是「产出满、废料空」的那幅图。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a worker whose desk and schedule leave no waste.

branches.en: THE POWER: both senses are about producing, one with economy and one in philosophy.
branches.cn: 力量线：两个义项都关乎「产生」，一个讲节省，一个讲哲学。

branches.en: THE HABIT: a person can be as efficient as a well-tuned machine.
branches.cn: 习惯线：人可以像调好的机器一样高效。

definition_zh: 元素；（构成整体的）要素；成分；少量；[the elements] 恶劣天气
definition_en: a simple chemical substance that cannot be split by chemical means, one part of a whole, a small amount of a quality, or the forces of weather
core_image: 摊开的元素周期表，一格一格印着字母符号
scene: 老师在黑板上画了一张表格，一格一格写着字母和数字。 Carbon is an element found in every living thing.
sceneCN: 这里 element 是「化学元素」（第 1 个义项：由同种原子构成、不能用化学方法再分的物质）；句意是碳是每个生物体内都能找到的元素。

pos.zh: 名词：元素；要素；成分；少量；[复数] 恶劣天气

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「基本的；自然力的；元素的」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ary 构成，义为「基础的；初级的」
由 elemental 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「基本地；以自然力地」

senses.title: A chemical element
senses.definition: a substance made of only one kind of atom, which cannot be broken down by chemical means
senses.definitionCN: 只由一种原子构成的物质，无法用化学方法再分
senses.example: Oxygen is the most common element in the earth's crust.
senses.exampleCN: 氧是地壳中含量最多的元素。
senses.why: Elementum first named a first principle, a unit you cannot go behind; chemistry kept exactly that role for the simplest substances.
senses.whyCN: elementum 最初指「不可再往前拆的第一原则」，化学把完全相同的角色留给了最简单的物质。

senses.title: A part of a whole
senses.definition: one of the parts or qualities that together make up a whole thing
senses.definitionCN: 共同构成某一整体的部分或性质之一
senses.example: Trust is a key element of any friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 信任是任何友谊的关键要素。
senses.why: If an element is an irreducible unit, then a complex thing is merely a set of such units, so the word names any necessary part.
senses.whyCN: 既然 element 是不可再分的单位，复杂事物就只是一组这样的单位，于是这个词指任何必要的组成部分。

senses.title: A small amount of a quality
senses.definition: a small but noticeable amount of a quality or feeling within something larger
senses.definitionCN: 某个较大事物中少量却可察觉的性质或情绪
senses.example: There is an element of truth in what she says.
senses.exampleCN: 她说的话里有几分道理。
senses.why: The irreducible unit can be tiny, so an element became a small measure of something mixed in.
senses.whyCN: 不可再分的单位可以很小，于是 element 变成掺在其中的一点分量。

senses.title: Wind rain and cold
senses.definition: the forces of weather, especially bad weather, used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 天气的力量，尤指恶劣天气，多用复数
senses.example: The tent kept out the elements.
senses.exampleCN: 这顶帐篷挡住了风吹雨打。
senses.why: The old four elements were earth, air, fire and water, and the open sky was thought to be their arena, so weather became the elements.
senses.whyCN: 古老的四元素是土、气、火、水，而开阔的天空被当作它们的战场，于是天气就成了 the elements。

intro.en: Element comes from Latin elementum, a word of debated origin meaning a first principle; note that the opening e- is part of the stem, not a prefix.
intro.cn: element 来自拉丁语 elementum，意为「第一原则」，其来源至今有争议；注意开头的 e- 属于词干本身，不是前缀。

items.en: Elementum named a first principle and also the letters of the alphabet, the units of writing.
items.cn: elementum 指第一原则，也指字母表里的字母，即书写的单位。

items.en: In the plural it named the four basic substances: earth, water, air and fire.
items.cn: 复数形式指四种基本物质：土、水、气、火。

items.en: French kept the word for a basic component of anything.
items.cn: 法语保留这个词，指任何事物的基本组成部分。

items.en: English used it for the four substances and for the parts of a whole.
items.cn: 英语用它指四种元素，也指整体的各个部分。

items.en: With modern chemistry the word was fixed to substances defined by atomic number.
items.cn: 随着近代化学的发展，这个词被固定给按原子序数定义的物质。

items.en: The weather sense survives in the plural, the quality sense in phrases like an element of truth.
items.cn: 天气义留在复数中，性质义留在 an element of truth 这类短语里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the element family; the near-meaning group separates a component, an ingredient, a factor and a substance.
note.cn: 形近组收 element 词族；近义组区分 component、ingredient、factor 与 substance。

entries.definition: Of the elements or of raw natural forces; basic and powerful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「基本的；自然力的」，带原始力量感。

entries.definition: At the simplest level; also the adjective for basic particles.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「基础的；初级的」，也用于基本粒子。

entries.definition: The plural, used for weather or for a set of basic parts.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，指恶劣天气或一组基本组成部分。

entries.definition: A part of a machine or system; more technical than element.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部件、组件」，比 element 更技术化。

entries.definition: One of the things mixed into a recipe or a product.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成分、配料」，指混进配方或产品里的东西。

entries.definition: One thing that influences a result; about causes rather than parts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「因素」，指影响结果的原因，而非组成的部分。

entries.definition: A material with a definite make-up; the physical side of the chemical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「物质」，是元素义在物理层面的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the word close to its Latin sense of a unit you cannot break, then spread that unit across chemistry, wholes and weather.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子让词义贴近拉丁语「拆不开的单位」，再把单位铺到化学、整体与天气上。

normal.en: The e- in element is not a prefix; elementum is one solid stem.
normal.cn: element 开头的 e- 不是前缀，elementum 整个是实心词干。

normal.en: A chemical element is the last stop: split it and it is no longer that element.
normal.cn: 化学 element 是终点：再分下去，它就不是那个元素了。

normal.en: An element of a plan is one brick that cannot be left out.
normal.cn: 计划里的一个 element，就是一块不能少的砖。

normal.en: An element of truth is a small piece that cannot be split further.
normal.cn: an element of truth 就是一粒再拆不开的真话。

normal.en: The weather outside is the elements because the sky was their arena.
normal.cn: 外面的天气叫 the elements，因为天空曾是四元素的战场。

abstract.en: Picture a table where every cell holds one letter and one number.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表格，每一格只装一个字母和一个数字。

abstract.en: Everything complicated is a stack of these single cells.
abstract.cn: 一切复杂的东西，都是这些单格堆起来的。

abstract.en: Element is the smallest block that still keeps its own name.
abstract.cn: element 是仍然保有自己名字的最小一块。

examples.en: Oxygen is the most common element in the earth's crust.
examples.cn: 氧是地壳中含量最多的元素。

examples.en: Trust is a key element of any friendship.
examples.cn: 信任是任何友谊的关键要素。

examples.en: There is an element of truth in what she says.
examples.cn: 她说的话里有几分道理。

root: 源自拉丁语 elementum「第一原则；字母」，来源有争议；开头的 e- 不是前缀，而是词干的一部分，与 elevate 的 e-（＝ex-）不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of element: the chemical substance, a necessary part, a small amount of a quality, and the weather in the plural.
sensesIntro.cn: element 的四个义项：化学元素、必要组成部分、少量的某种性质，以及复数形式的恶劣天气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a periodic table whose cells each hold one letter and one number.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张周期表，每格只装一个字母和一个数字。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: one kind of atom, named by number.
branches.cn: 物质线：一种原子，以序数命名。

branches.en: THE PART: a unit that a whole cannot do without.
branches.cn: 部分线：整体少不了的那个单位。

branches.en: THE TRACE: the same unit shrunk to a hint.
branches.cn: 微量线：同一个单位缩小成一缕线索。

branches.en: THE WEATHER: the old four elements turned into sky.
branches.cn: 天气线：古老的四元素化作头顶的天空。

branches.en: THE TABLE: chemistry and plain parts share one word.
branches.cn: 表格线：化学与日常的「部分」共用一个词。

intro.en: Element has no prefix: the whole word is the Latin stem elementum, and the -ment at the end is a worn-down ending rather than the English suffix.
intro.cn: element 没有前缀：整个词就是拉丁词干 elementum，末尾的 -ment 是磨损后的词尾，不是英语后缀 -ment。

latinIntro.en: Elementum and its plural elementa are recorded Latin forms; the word's deeper origin is still disputed.
latinIntro.cn: elementum 及其复数 elementa 是有记录的拉丁语形式；这个词更深的来源至今仍有争议。

items.example: It is borrowed with little change.

items.meaningCN: 磨损的拉丁词尾，并非后缀

definition_zh: 作者，作家；发起者，创始人；撰写，创作
definition_en: a person who writes a book or other work, the person who started a plan or idea, or to write something
core_image: 书页最上方印着一个人的名字，下面才是正文
scene: 新书发布会上，主持人请写这本书的人先讲两句。 The author signed copies for two hours.
sceneCN: 这里 author 是「作者、作家」（第 1 个义项）；句意是作者签了两个小时的书。

senses.title: Writer of a work
senses.definition: a person who writes a book, article or other text
senses.definitionCN: 写书、写文章或其他文字作品的人
senses.example: The author signed copies for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 作者签了两个小时的书。
senses.why: The Latin source auctor meant an originator, so the writer is seen as the person from whom the text comes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 auctor 意为「开创者」，所以作者被视为文本从之而来的那个人。

senses.title: Person who started something
senses.definition: the person who first thought of or started a plan, idea or change
senses.definitionCN: 最先想到或发起某个计划、想法、变革的人
senses.example: She is the author of the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这场改革的发起者。
senses.why: The word keeps its older sense of originator: nothing needs to be written down for someone to be the author of a plan.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留了「开创者」的旧义：要成为一项计划的发起者，并不需要真的写下什么。

senses.title: Write something
senses.definition: to write a book, report or other work yourself
senses.definitionCN: 亲自写出书、报告或其他作品
senses.example: He authored three reports on the case.
senses.exampleCN: 他就这个案子撰写了三份报告。
senses.why: The verb is modern and slightly formal; it stresses who produced the text rather than the act of writing itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词用法较新且偏正式，强调的是文本由谁产出，而不是书写这个动作本身。

intro.en: Author and authority grow from the same Latin word for an originator.
intro.cn: author 与 authority 出自同一个表示「开创者」的拉丁词。

items.en: augere meant 'to increase or make grow'.
items.cn: augere 意为「增加、使生长」。

items.en: auctor meant 'originator, promoter or seller'.
items.cn: auctor 意为「开创者、推动者、让与者」。

items.en: autor named the writer of a work.
items.cn: 古法语 autor 指作品的写作者。

items.en: English author covered both writer and founder.
items.cn: 中古英语 author 兼指写作者与创立者。

items.en: A verb use appeared, meaning to write a work.
items.cn: 现代英语又出现动词用法，意为撰写作品。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the auctor root; the near-meaning group gives words for writers and creators.
note.cn: 形近组共享 auctor 词根；近义组是表示写作者与创造者的词。

normalIntro.en: An author is where a text or a plan begins.
normalIntro.cn: author 就是文本或计划的起点。

normal.en: The root auctor means originator, which is why a plan can have an author.
normal.cn: 词根 auctor 意为开创者，所以一项计划也能有 author。

normal.en: The noun is common; the verb is formal and usually about reports or books.
normal.cn: 名词很常见；动词偏正式，多用于报告或书。

normal.en: Authority is not a person but the power an author figure holds.
normal.cn: authority 不是人，而是作者式人物握有的权力。

normal.en: Co-author adds co- for a shared writer.
normal.cn: co-author 加 co- 表示共同写作的人。

normal.en: Authorship names the fact of being the author.
normal.cn: authorship 指作者身份这件事。

abstract.en: See a name printed above the title on a first page.
abstract.cn: 想象扉页上书名上方印着一个名字。

abstract.en: See a hand writing the last line and putting down the pen.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手写完最后一行，把笔放下。

abstract.en: See a blueprint with one signature in the corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一张蓝图，角落里有一个人签名。

definition_zh: 衣柜；衣橱；（某人的）全部服装；戏服；（剧院的）服装部
definition_en: a tall cabinet for hanging clothes, or all the clothes that a person owns
core_image: 一扇高柜的门：关在里面的一整座「衣之王国」
scene: 清晨的卧室，柜门开着，衣服挂得整整齐齐。 She packed the whole wardrobe into two suitcases when she moved abroad.
sceneCN: 这里 wardrobe 是「全部服装」（第 2 个义项：一个人拥有的所有衣服）；句意是她出国时把整套衣物装进两只行李箱。

pos.zh: 名词：衣柜；衣橱；全部服装；戏服

derivatives.zh: 名词短语，义为「（剧院）服装管理员」，由 wardrobe 加 mistress 构成

名词，义为「看守、管理员」，与 wardrobe 同出「守护」词根

senses.title: A cabinet for clothes
senses.definition: a tall piece of furniture with doors, used for hanging and storing clothes
senses.definitionCN: 带柜门的高大家具，用于悬挂和存放衣物
senses.example: The old wardrobe creaked whenever its door opened.
senses.exampleCN: 那口旧衣柜的门一开就吱呀作响。
senses.why: Old French warderobe means a guarded robe place: the room where robes were kept under watch.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 warderobe 意为「守衣之处」：即被看守存放长袍的房间。

senses.title: All the clothes a person has
senses.titleCN: 全部服装：一个人的整套衣装
senses.definition: the collection of clothes owned by a person
senses.definitionCN: 一个人拥有的所有衣服的总称
senses.example: She packed the whole wardrobe into two suitcases when she moved abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 出国时她把整套衣物装进了两只行李箱。
senses.why: The guarded room holds every robe; the place's contents become the person's clothes.
senses.whyCN: 守衣之屋装着所有长袍，这个地方的藏品便成了一个人的全部衣装。

senses.title: Theatrical costumes
senses.titleCN: 戏服：剧场与影视的服装
senses.definition: the costumes of a theater or film production, or the department that keeps them
senses.definitionCN: 剧场或影视制作中的服装，或保管它们的部门
senses.example: The wardrobe team stitched the king's cloak overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 服装部连夜缝好了国王的斗篷。
senses.why: The room that once kept nobles' robes now keeps actors' costumes.
senses.whyCN: 昔日存放贵族长袍的房间，如今保管演员的戏服。

senses.title: Costumes of a period or role
senses.titleCN: 行头：特定时期或角色的一套装扮
senses.definition: the set of clothes appropriate to a period, activity, or role
senses.definitionCN: 适合某个时期、活动或角色的一套衣着
senses.example: His winter wardrobe is mostly grey wool.
senses.exampleCN: 他的冬季行头大多是灰色呢料。
senses.why: One guarded room per need: each season and role keeps its own robes.
senses.whyCN: 每种需求各有自己的守衣之屋：每个季节、每个角色都存着自己的行头。

intro.en: Wardrobe comes from Old French warderobe or garderobe, literally a place where robes are guarded, from Germanic warder, to guard, plus robe.
intro.cn: wardrobe 源自古法语 warderobe 或 garderobe，字面为「看守长袍之处」，由日耳曼语 warder（看守）加 robe（长袍）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ward- means to guard or watch over.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ward- 意为看守、守卫。

items.en: Warderobe and garderobe name both the guarded room for robes and the robes themselves.
items.cn: 古法语 warderobe、garderobe 兼指存放长袍的守卫室与这些长袍。

items.en: Middle English borrows wardrobe first as the room where robes were stored, often near the king's chamber.
items.cn: 14 世纪，中古英语借入 wardrobe，先指存放长袍的房间，常设在王室寝殿附近。

items.en: The sense narrows to the standing cabinet for clothes in ordinary houses.
items.cn: 15 至 17 世纪，词义收窄为普通民居中存放衣物的立柜。

items.en: The collective sense grows: a person's wardrobe becomes all the clothes they own.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪，集合义生长：一个人的 wardrobe 成为其全部衣装。

items.en: Wardrobe now spans furniture, clothes collections, and theatrical costume departments.
items.cn: 如今 wardrobe 涵盖家具、衣装总集与剧场服装部门。

note.en: Wardrobe stands inside the Germanic guard-family joined to French robe; look-alikes share the guard-root, near meanings share the field of storing and clothing.
note.cn: wardrobe 处于日耳曼「守护」词根与法语 robe 的结合处：形近组共享词根，近义组共享「储物与衣着」义场。

entries.definition: to guard; a person under guard; a hospital room
entries.definitionCN: 看守、受监护人、病房；与 wardrobe 同出「守护」词根 warder

entries.definition: a keeper of a prison, college, or building
entries.definitionCN: 看守长、管理员；同根词

entries.definition: a guard, especially a prison guard
entries.definitionCN: 狱吏；wardrobe 词首 warder 即出自此词

entries.definition: a fighter
entries.definitionCN: 武士；与 wardrobe 词首拼形相近，但源自法语 guerre（战争），词根不同

entries.definition: a medieval robe-room, later a privy
entries.definitionCN: 中世纪的守衣室，后转指厕所；garderobe 与 wardrobe 是法语孪生

entries.definition: a small room or cabinet for storing things
entries.definitionCN: 壁橱、小储物间；美式常用词

entries.definition: garments worn on the body
entries.definitionCN: 衣服；wardrobe 的集合义与之相当但更正式

entries.definition: clothes, especially of a specified type
entries.definitionCN: 服饰、着装；正式用语

entries.definition: a set of clothes worn for a role or period
entries.definitionCN: 戏装、特定场合的装束；与戏服义相邻

entries.definition: a cabinet of drawers for folded clothes
entries.definitionCN: 五斗柜；存放叠放衣物，与挂衣的 wardrobe 分工不同

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the guard-root warder and the French robe.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，来自「守护」词根 warder 与法语 robe（长袍）。

normal.en: warder means guard; a wardrobe is literally a guarded robe place.
normal.cn: warder 意为看守；wardrobe 字面就是「被看守的长袍之处」。

normal.en: ward and wardrobe share the same Germanic guard-root.
normal.cn: ward 与 wardrobe 共享同一日耳曼守护词根。

normal.en: garderobe is the French twin with g instead of w.
normal.cn: garderobe 是法语孪生词，把 w 换成 g。

normal.en: robe itself means a long garment, and it still lives in English.
normal.cn: robe 本义为长袍，在英语中至今沿用。

normal.en: capsule wardrobe is a modern fixed phrase for a minimal clothes set.
normal.cn: capsule wardrobe（极简衣橱）是现代固定说法，指一小组百搭衣物。

abstract.en: A tall door opens and a whole season of mornings hangs inside.
abstract.cn: 高高的柜门打开，一整个季节的清晨挂在里面。

abstract.en: A guard stands in a small stone room where kings' robes rest, folded and counted.
abstract.cn: 小石室里站着卫兵，国王的长袍叠好存放在此，一一清点。

abstract.en: Every person owns one invisible room where all their clothes live together.
abstract.cn: 每人心里都有一间看不见的房间，所有的衣服在那里同住。

examples.en: A wardrobe stood against the wall of the small bedroom.
examples.cn: 小卧室的墙边立着一口衣柜。

examples.en: A capsule wardrobe of ten pieces can cover every occasion.
examples.cn: 十件单品组成的极简衣橱就能应对各种场合。

examples.en: Backstage, the wardrobe crew was still sewing sequins onto the dresses.
examples.cn: 后台，服装组的成员还在往裙子上缝亮片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我捉漏」——衣柜门没关严，风一吹衣架「捉漏捉漏」地晃。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自古法语 warderobe（守衣之处）。

root: 日耳曼语词根 *ward-（看守）→ 法语动词 warder（看守）+ robe（长袍）构成古法语 warderobe（守衣之处）→ 中古英语 wardrobe（存衣房间→立柜→全部衣装）。garderobe 是其法语孪生形式。robe 继续生活于英语 robe（长袍、浴袍）。核心意象是「被看护的衣装」。

sensesIntro.en: From the guarded robe-room outward: the cabinet, the whole collection of clothes, theatrical costumes, and the set for one season or role.
sensesIntro.cn: 从守衣之屋向外铺开：立柜、全部衣装、剧场戏服，最后到某季某角色的整套行头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: robes kept safe behind a guarded door
core.cn: 核心意象：长袍被妥帖地收在有人看守的门后

branches.en: The room hardened into furniture: the cabinet itself
branches.cn: 房间凝固为家具：立柜本身

branches.en: The contents become the person's whole clothing
branches.cn: 藏品化作一个人的全部衣装

branches.en: The guarded room now serves the stage
branches.cn: 守衣之屋如今为舞台服务

branches.en: One room per need: seasons and roles keep their own robes
branches.cn: 每种需求一间屋：季节与角色各存其衣

branches.en: From kings' robes to actors' cloaks, the keeper stays the same
branches.cn: 从国王的长袍到演员的斗篷，看守始终未变

intro.en: Wardrobe is itself a compound: a Germanic guard-verb joined to a French garment noun.
intro.cn: wardrobe 本身就是复合词：日耳曼守护动词接上法语衣装名词。

latinIntro.en: This family is Germanic-French mixed; Latin has no direct cognate here.
latinIntro.cn: 此词族是日耳曼与法语的混合来源，此处没有直接的拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: the costume section of a production

items.meaningCN: 看守；受监护人（同根近亲）

derivatives.zh: 服装管理员，由 wardrobe 加 mistress 构成
狱吏，与 wardrobe 同根的看守者
管理员，与 wardrobe 同根的看守长

definition_zh: 情感；情绪；感情
definition_en: a strong feeling such as love, anger or fear; a state of mental agitation
core_image: 心里有什么被搅动起来，一路涌到脸上
scene: 听到消息，她握着电话半天没说出话。 Her voice shook with emotion.
sceneCN: 这里 emotion 是「情感、情绪」（第 01 个义项：强烈的内心感受）；句意是她的声音因情绪而发抖。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -al 构成，义为「情感的；情绪化的」
由 emotional 加 -ly 构成，义为「情感上地」
由词干加 -ive 构成，义为「引起强烈情感的」

senses.title: A strong feeling
senses.definition: a strong feeling such as love, anger, fear or joy
senses.definitionCN: 爱、怒、惧、喜等强烈的内心感受
senses.example: Her voice shook with emotion.
senses.exampleCN: 她的声音因情绪而发抖。
senses.why: The word comes from a verb meaning to move out, so an emotion is something stirred up inside and pushing outward.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自表示「向外移动」的动词，所以 emotion 就是心里被搅动起来、并向外推的东西。

senses.title: A particular feeling
senses.definition: one specific feeling, such as guilt, pride or grief
senses.definitionCN: 某一种具体的感受，如内疚、骄傲或悲伤
senses.example: He could not name the emotion he felt.
senses.exampleCN: 他说不出自己感受到的是哪种情绪。
senses.why: The general stirring can be divided into named kinds, so the same noun also counts individual feelings one by one.
senses.whyCN: 笼统的搅动可以分成分门别类的几种，于是同一个名词也用来逐一计数具体情绪。

senses.title: Mental agitation, in formal use
senses.definition: a disturbed or excited state of mind, often contrasted with calm reason
senses.definitionCN: 心绪受扰或兴奋的状态，常与冷静理性相对
senses.example: The speech appealed to emotion rather than reason.
senses.exampleCN: 那场演讲诉诸情感而非理性。
senses.why: When feelings are stirred strongly, they can override calm thought, so emotion also names agitation as a force opposed to reason.
senses.whyCN: 当感受被强烈搅动时，会压过冷静思考，所以 emotion 也指一股与理性相对抗的激动力量。

intro.en: Emotion entered English through French and ultimately goes back to a Latin verb meaning to move out.
intro.cn: emotion 经法语进入英语，最终可追溯到表示「向外移动」的拉丁语动词。

items.en: Movere meant to move or stir.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、搅动。

items.en: With e-, out, the verb meant to move out or stir up.
items.cn: 加上 e-（向外）后，动词意为移出、激起。

items.en: Esmovoir and later emouvoir carried the sense of stirring feelings.
items.cn: esmovoir 及后来的 emouvoir 带有「搅动感情」的意思。

items.en: The noun named a stirring of the mind.
items.cn: 名词 émotion 指心绪被搅动。

items.en: English emotion settled on strong feeling and later on specific feelings.
items.cn: 英语 emotion 先固定为强烈感受，后又指具体情绪。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the emotion family; the near-meaning group separates feeling, sentiment and passion.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 emotion 词族展开；近义组区分感受、情感与激情。

entries.definition: Relating to or showing emotion.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「情感的、情绪化的」。

entries.definition: In an emotional way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在情感上」。

entries.definition: Arousing strong feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「引起强烈情感的」。

entries.definition: A general word for an inner sensation or attitude.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「感觉、感受」，是最宽泛的说法。

entries.definition: A view or feeling, often a refined or expressed one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「情感、观点」，常指较细腻或被表达出的感受。

entries.definition: A very strong emotion, especially love or anger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「激情」，强度高于一般 emotion。

normalIntro.en: These hooks read emotion as movement out of the mind, then let the stirring become a named feeling or a force against reason.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 emotion 读成「从心里往外移动」，再让这次搅动变成具体情绪或对抗理性的力量。

normal.en: E- out plus mov move: something stirred out.
normal.cn: e- 向外加 mov 移动：有东西被搅动着往外走。

normal.en: Strong emotion can shake a voice.
normal.cn: 强烈的情感能让声音发抖。

normal.en: Mixed emotions are several feelings at once.
normal.cn: mixed emotions 就是几种感受同时出现。

normal.en: Emotional is the adjective made with -al.
normal.cn: emotional 是加 -al 构成的形容词。

normal.en: An appeal to emotion opposes an appeal to reason.
normal.cn: 诉诸情感与诉诸理性相对。

abstract.en: Picture a still pond stirred by a hand from below.
abstract.cn: 想象一潭静水被水下的一只手搅动。

abstract.en: The word is movement first and a name for feelings second.
abstract.cn: 这个词先是「移动」，后来才成为感受的名字。

abstract.en: Emotion is weather inside a person.
abstract.cn: emotion 就是一个人内部的天气。

examples.en: Her voice shook with emotion.
examples.cn: 她的声音因情绪而发抖。

examples.en: He could not name the emotion he felt.
examples.cn: 他说不出自己感受到的是哪种情绪。

examples.en: The speech appealed to emotion rather than reason.
examples.cn: 那场演讲诉诸情感而非理性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一摸神」——心里被摸了一下，神情立刻变了

root: 经法语 émotion 借入，源头为拉丁语 emovere，由 e-（向外）加 movere（移动、搅动）构成，字面为「把心绪搅动出来」。

sensesIntro.en: Emotion is a stirred feeling in general, then one named feeling, then agitation set against calm reason.
sensesIntro.cn: emotion 先指被搅动的强烈感受，再指某一种具体情绪，最后指与冷静理性相对的激动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something stirring inside a person and rising to the face.
core.cn: 核心意象：心里有东西被搅动，一路涌到脸上。

branches.en: THE STIRRING: strong feeling in general.
branches.cn: 搅动线：泛指强烈感受。

branches.en: THE NAME: one specific feeling such as grief.
branches.cn: 名称线：某种具体情绪，如悲伤。

branches.en: THE FORCE: agitation opposed to calm thought.
branches.cn: 力量线：与冷静思考相对的激动。

branches.en: MASS AND UNIT: the general sea and one wave.
branches.cn: 整体与单数：整片海与一朵浪。

branches.en: FEELING AND POWER: the same stir can move or overpower.
branches.cn: 感受与力量：同一次搅动既能打动，也能压倒。

intro.en: Emotion is a French borrowing whose -ion names a state; its English family adds -al, -ally and -ive.
intro.cn: emotion 是法语借词，其中的 -ion 表示状态；英语词族又加 -al、-ally 与 -ive。

latinIntro.en: Movere and emovere are recorded Latin verbs of moving and stirring.
latinIntro.cn: movere 与 emovere 都是有记录的拉丁语动词，表示移动与搅动。

derivatives.zh: 情感的；情绪化的
在情感上
引起强烈情感的

definition_zh: 故意地；从容地
definition_en: on purpose, or in a slow and calm way
core_image: 一只手慢慢伸出去，明知会碰倒仍不收回
scene: 他把最后一道题空着交上去，走出考场时脚步很稳。 He deliberately left the last question unanswered.
sceneCN: 这里 deliberately 指「故意地」（第 1 个义项：有意识地这么做）；句意是他故意把最后一题留空。

derivatives.zh: 故意的；从容的
商议；审慎
审议性的
有意；从容

senses.title: With full intention
senses.definition: with the full knowledge that one is doing it
senses.definitionCN: 完全知道自己正在这么做
senses.example: He deliberately left the last question unanswered.
senses.exampleCN: 他故意把最后一题留空。
senses.why: A hand that does not shake shows the mind has already decided.
senses.whyCN: 手不发抖，说明心里早就定了。

senses.title: Without any hurry
senses.definition: in a slow, steady and calm manner
senses.definitionCN: 以缓慢、平稳而镇定的方式
senses.example: She closed the book deliberately and stood up.
senses.exampleCN: 她不慌不忙地合上书，站起身来。
senses.why: Slowness can be a form of control, not a lack of it.
senses.whyCN: 慢也可以是一种掌控，而不是失控。

intro.en: Deliberately is deliberate plus -ly, and deliberate goes back to Latin libra, a balance.
intro.cn: deliberately 是 deliberate 加 -ly，而 deliberate 上溯到拉丁语的 libra（天平）。

items.en: Libra was the scale used to weigh goods.
items.cn: libra 是称货用的天平。

items.en: Deliberare meant to weigh a matter before acting.
items.cn: deliberare 意为行动前先把事情称一称。

items.en: English kept the picture of a slow and careful mind.
items.cn: 英语保留了那种缓慢而小心的画面。

items.en: The adverb marked acts that were clearly intended.
items.cn: 副词形式用来标示明显有意的行为。

items.en: Today it can accuse and admire in the same breath.
items.cn: 如今它既可用于指责，也可用于赞赏。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deliberate stem, and the meaning group offers three ways to say it was no accident.
note.cn: 形近组共用 deliberate 这个词干，近义组则给出三种「不是意外」的说法。

entries.definition: done on purpose and after thought
entries.definitionCN: 有意的、经过考虑的

entries.definition: long and careful discussion
entries.definitionCN: 长时间的仔细讨论

entries.definition: in a gentle and careful way
entries.definitionCN: 以轻柔小心的方式

entries.definition: with the purpose of doing it
entries.definitionCN: 带着这样的目的去做

entries.definition: for a set reason, not by chance
entries.definitionCN: 出于既定理由，而非偶然

entries.definition: while fully aware of what one does
entries.definitionCN: 完全清楚自己在做什么

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a blank answer on a test paper and end with a hand that closes a book slowly.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从考卷上一处空白开始，落到一只慢慢合上书的手。

normal.en: A blank left on purpose is still an answer.
normal.cn: 有意留出的空白，也是一种回答。

normal.en: The steadiest hand in the room has already decided.
normal.cn: 屋里最稳的那只手，早就做好了决定。

normal.en: To be vague on purpose is to hide behind fog you made.
normal.cn: 故意含糊，就是躲进自己造的雾里。

normal.en: Slow steps are not weak steps.
normal.cn: 慢的脚步，不是弱的脚步。

normal.en: Deliberate plus -ly turns a weighing mind into a manner.
normal.cn: deliberate 加 -ly，称量的心思就变成了举止。

abstract.en: Picture a pen lifted just before it touches the paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔在碰到纸之前停住。

abstract.en: Picture a door held open for no one in particular.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被扶着，谁也没在过。

abstract.en: Picture two eyes meeting yours and not looking away.
abstract.cn: 想象一双眼睛对上你的，没有躲开。

examples.en: He deliberately left the last question unanswered.
examples.cn: 他故意把最后一题留空。

examples.en: She closed the book deliberately and stood up.
examples.cn: 她不慌不忙地合上书，站起身来。

examples.en: The report was deliberately vague about the date.
examples.cn: 报告在日期上故意写得含糊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deliberately 记成「地里有谱」：心里早有谱，才做得不慌不忙，也都是故意为之。

root: 由 deliberate 加副词词尾 -ly 构成。deliberate 出自拉丁语 deliberare，词根 libra 是天平，本义是称量、权衡。称过的举动是有意的，称的过程是缓慢的，所以这个词同时表示「故意地」与「从容地」。

sensesIntro.en: From an act nobody can call accidental, to a pace nobody can call hurried.
sensesIntro.cn: 从没人能说是意外的举动，到没人能说是匆忙的步调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steady hand that does not stop itself.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只稳稳伸出、并不收回的手。

branches.en: The first sense removes any excuse of accident.
branches.cn: 第一个义项排除了「不小心」这个借口。

branches.en: The second sense is the same control shown in speed.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是同样的掌控体现在速度上。

branches.en: Both senses come from a mind that has already weighed the matter.
branches.cn: 两个义项都出自一颗已经称量过的心。

branches.en: Deliberately in a charge sheet means the act was chosen.
branches.cn: 在指控里说故意，意思是这行为是选出来的。

branches.en: In praise, deliberately means nothing was rushed or wasted.
branches.cn: 在称赞里，它意味着没有一样东西被赶出来或浪费掉。

intro.en: Deliberately sits at the adverb end of the deliberate family, next to deliberation and deliberative.
intro.cn: deliberately 站在 deliberate 这一族的副词一端，旁边是 deliberation 与 deliberative。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is libra, a balance, with de- meaning thoroughly.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 libra（天平），前缀 de- 表示彻底。

items.example: He deliberately took the longer road.
items.exampleCN: 他故意走了更远的那条路。

items.example: They met in a deliberative mood.
items.exampleCN: 他们带着审议的心情开会。

items.example: The deliberateness of the silence was plain.
items.exampleCN: 那片沉默显然是有意的。
那封信被故意搁着不理。

definition_zh: 保卫；为…辩护；防守
definition_en: to protect someone or something from attack, or to speak in support of a person or idea
core_image: 一个人挡在门口，把身后的人护住
scene: 球门前的守门员张开双臂，用身体挡住了近角。 The keeper defended the near post with his body.
sceneCN: 这里 defend 指「防守」（第 1 个义项：保护位置不受攻击）；句意是守门员用身体守住了近角。

derivatives.zh: 防御；辩护
守卫者；辩护人
防御性的
可辩护的
无人防守的

senses.title: Keep someone safe from attack
senses.definition: to protect a person or place from harm or attack
senses.definitionCN: 保护人或地点免受伤害或攻击
senses.example: Two soldiers defended the bridge all night.
senses.exampleCN: 两名士兵整夜守着那座桥。
senses.why: To defend is to put your own body where the blow is going.
senses.whyCN: 保卫就是把自己的身体放到打击落下的地方。

senses.title: Speak up for a person or idea
senses.definition: to argue in support of someone or something that is criticized
senses.definitionCN: 为受到批评的人或事提出支持的理由
senses.example: She defended her decision at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她在会上为自己的决定辩护。
senses.why: Words can stand in front of a person just as a body can.
senses.whyCN: 言语也能像身体一样，站在一个人前面。

senses.title: Hold a position in sport
senses.definition: to try to stop the other side from scoring or from taking a title
senses.definitionCN: 努力阻止对方得分或夺走头衔
senses.example: The champion defended his title in three sets.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军用三盘守住了自己的头衔。
senses.why: A title is a place, and places must be held.
senses.whyCN: 头衔就是一个位置，而位置总要有人守。

intro.en: Defend comes from Latin defendere, to strike away, made of de- away and -fendere to strike.
intro.cn: defend 来自拉丁语 defendere（把打击挡开），由 de-（离开）与 -fendere（击打）组成。

items.en: Defendere first described pushing a weapon aside.
items.cn: defendere 最初指把兵器推开。

items.en: In law it came to mean speaking for the accused.
items.cn: 在法律里，它逐渐指替被告说话。

items.en: Defendre carried both senses into French.
items.cn: defendre 把这两层意思带进法语。

items.en: English kept the double meaning of body and speech.
items.cn: 英语同时保留了身体与言语两种意思。

items.en: Now a team defends a lead and a writer defends an idea.
items.cn: 如今球队守领先优势，作者也维护自己的观点。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the defe- shape, and the meaning group moves from shielding to justifying.
note.cn: 形近组共用 defe- 这个形状，近义组则从护住一路走到讲出理由。

entries.definition: to win against an opponent
entries.definitionCN: 战胜对手

entries.definition: to state the exact meaning of a word
entries.definitionCN: 说明一个词的确切含义

entries.definition: to put something off to a later time
entries.definitionCN: 把某事推迟到以后

entries.definition: to keep someone from harm
entries.definitionCN: 使某人不受伤害

entries.definition: to put something between a person and danger
entries.definitionCN: 在人与危险之间放上东西

entries.definition: to show that something is reasonable
entries.definitionCN: 说明某事是合理的

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a body in a doorway and end with a sentence spoken on someone's behalf.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从门口的一具身体开始，落到替人说出的一句话。

normal.en: A door is only a door if someone is willing to stand in it.
normal.cn: 门之所以是门，是因为有人肯站在那儿。

normal.en: A goalkeeper is a wall that can move.
normal.cn: 守门员是一堵会动的墙。

normal.en: When a friend is blamed, your voice becomes his shield.
normal.cn: 朋友被指责时，你的声音就是他的盾。

normal.en: You cannot defend a title you are not willing to hold.
normal.cn: 不肯守住的位置，就守不住头衔。

normal.en: Defend and defence differ only by the ending you choose.
normal.cn: defend 与 defence 只差一个词尾。

abstract.en: Picture a shoulder turned toward a coming blow.
abstract.cn: 想象一个肩膀转向即将落下的打击。

abstract.en: Picture one hand raised flat to stop a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手平举起来，拦住人群。

abstract.en: Picture a quiet voice saying one firm sentence in a loud room.
abstract.cn: 想象喧闹屋里一个安静的声音说出一句坚定的话。

examples.en: Two soldiers defended the bridge all night.
examples.cn: 两名士兵整夜守着那座桥。

examples.en: She defended her decision at the meeting.
examples.cn: 她在会上为自己的决定辩护。

examples.en: The champion defended his title in three sets.
examples.cn: 冠军用三盘守住了自己的头衔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 defend 记成「挡风」：de 开头，fend 听起来像「风」，挡在风口上，就是保卫。

root: 源自拉丁语 defendere，本义是把打来的兵器推开，由 de-（离开）与 -fendere（击打）合成；经古法语 defendre 进入英语。它从一开始就带着两条线：用身体挡，和用言语挡，所以既能守桥，也能替人申辩。

sensesIntro.en: From a guard at a bridge, to a voice in a meeting, to a champion holding a title.
sensesIntro.cn: 从守在桥头的士兵，到会上发言的声音，再到守住头衔的冠军。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing in a doorway, arms open.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在门口，张开双臂。

branches.en: The first sense is a body placed between danger and another person.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把身体放在危险与别人之间。

branches.en: The same place, taken by words, answers a criticism.
branches.cn: 同样的位置由言语来占，就是回应指责。

branches.en: On a field, the place to hold is a lead or a title.
branches.cn: 在赛场上要守住的位置，是领先或头衔。

branches.en: Shield and argument are the same stance in different material.
branches.cn: 盾与辩词是同一种姿态，只是材料不同。

branches.en: Both senses are about not giving up what one already has.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是不肯让出已有的东西。

intro.en: Defend has a large family of nouns for guards, arguments and the act itself.
intro.cn: defend 的家族不小，有表示守卫者、辩护与防守行为的名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is -fendere, to strike, with de- meaning away.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 -fendere（击打），前缀 de- 表示离开。

items.example: They defended the town for a week.
The defence of the coast cost much.
He was a defender of free speech.
items.exampleCN: 他是言论自由的捍卫者。

definition_zh: 设施；设备；能力；便利
definition_en: a place or piece of equipment built for a purpose; an ability to do something easily; the quality of being easy to do
core_image: 一个让事情做起来更省力的装置或场所
scene: 这所学校有现代化的体育设施。 The school has modern sports facilities.
sceneCN: 这里 facility 是「设施、设备」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这所学校有现代化的体育设施。

derivatives.zh: 促进；使便利
促进者；协调人
容易的；肤浅的

senses.title: A built place or equipment
senses.definition: a place, building, or piece of equipment built for a particular purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为特定目的建造的场所、建筑或设备
senses.example: The hotel has excellent sports facilities.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店有极好的体育设施。
senses.why: The core sense is something made to make an activity possible.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是为使某项活动成为可能而建造的东西。

senses.title: An easy ability
senses.definition: a natural or learned ability to do something easily
senses.definitionCN: 轻松做某事的天生或习得能力
senses.example: She has a facility for learning languages.
senses.exampleCN: 她有学习语言的天赋。
senses.why: The made thing becomes a mental tool that makes action easy.
senses.whyCN: 人造之物变成使行动轻松的心智工具。

senses.title: Ease in doing
senses.definition: the quality of being easy to do or use
senses.definitionCN: 容易做或容易使用的性质
senses.example: He answered the questions with facility.
senses.exampleCN: 他轻松地回答了问题。
senses.why: The idea of ease is the abstract side of the same root.
senses.whyCN: 「容易」是同一词根的抽象一面。

intro.en: Facility comes from Latin facilitas, ease, from facilis, easy.
intro.cn: facility 来自拉丁语 facilitas（容易），源头是 facilis（容易的）。

items.en: Facilis means easy to do.
items.cn: facilis 意为容易做的。

items.en: Facilitas means ease or readiness.
items.cn: facilitas 意为容易或敏捷。

items.en: Facilite carries the sense of ease.
items.cn: facilite 带有轻松之义。

items.en: Facility comes to name buildings and equipment.
items.cn: 现代英语中 facility 转而指建筑与设备。

items.en: Facilities usually means a set of services.
items.cn: 当代英语中 facilities 通常指一整套服务设施。

note.en: Facility is a place or ease; faculty is an ability or department.
note.cn: facility 是设施或便利，faculty 则是能力或院系。

entries.definition: an ability or an academic department
entries.definitionCN: 能力；院系

entries.definition: too easy or superficial
entries.definitionCN: 容易的；肤浅的

entries.definition: great happiness or aptness
entries.definitionCN: 幸福；恰当

entries.definition: a useful or pleasant facility
entries.definitionCN: 便利设施

entries.definition: the things needed for an activity
entries.definitionCN: 设备；装备

entries.definition: the absence of difficulty
entries.definitionCN: 容易；轻松

normalIntro.en: Facility covers both the place that helps you and the ease you feel.
normalIntro.cn: facility 既指帮助你的设施，也指你感到的轻松。

normal.en: The campus has excellent library facilities.
normal.cn: 校园有极好的图书馆设施。

normal.en: The clinic lacks basic medical facilities.
normal.cn: 这家诊所缺乏基本医疗设施。

normal.en: She has a facility for remembering names.
normal.cn: 她记名字很有天赋。

normal.en: The new software improves facility of use.
normal.cn: 新软件提升了使用的便利性。

normal.en: They toured the research facility.
normal.cn: 他们参观了研究设施。

abstract.en: Picture a smooth ramp that makes a hard climb easy.
abstract.cn: 想象一条让艰难攀爬变轻松的平滑坡道。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand that finds every task light.
abstract.cn: 想象一只把每件事都做得轻松的手。

abstract.en: Think of a well-equipped room waiting to be used.
abstract.cn: 想象一间设备齐全、随时可用的房间。

examples.en: The city built new facilities for cyclists.
examples.cn: 这座城市为骑行者建造了新设施。

examples.en: His facility with numbers impressed the team.
examples.cn: 他对数字的敏锐让团队印象深刻。

examples.en: The task was completed with surprising facility.
examples.cn: 这项任务完成得异常轻松。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 拉丁词根
dict_mnemonic.text: facility 与 facile、facilitate 同源于拉丁语 facilis（容易的），凡是「设施」都是为了让事情更容易。

root: facility 源自拉丁语 facilitas（容易），来自 facilis（容易的），与 facilitate、facile 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Facility is a built place or equipment, an easy ability, or the quality of ease.
sensesIntro.cn: facility 指建成的设施设备、轻松的能力，或容易的性质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something that makes a task easier.
core.cn: 核心意象：让任务变得更轻松的东西。

branches.en: The base sense is the built place or equipment.
branches.cn: 基础义是建成的场所或设备。

branches.en: The tool becomes a mental ability.
branches.cn: 工具引申为心智能力。

branches.en: Ease is the abstract quality behind both.
branches.cn: 容易是两者背后的抽象性质。

branches.en: Both remove difficulty from an activity.
branches.cn: 两者都消除活动的难度。

branches.en: An ability is shown by acting with ease.
branches.cn: 能力体现为轻松地行动。

intro.en: Facility belongs to the fac- family of Latin origin meaning to do or make.
intro.cn: facility 属于源自拉丁语、意为「做或制造」的 fac- 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere, facilis, and facilitas explain this word family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere、facilis 与 facilitas 解释了这个词族。

items.meaning: services and equipment for a purpose

items.exampleCN: 这个应用促进了团队合作。

items.meaning: one who makes a process easier
items.example: The facilitator kept the meeting on track.
items.exampleCN: 协调人让会议保持正轨。

items.example: The sports facility has a pool.
items.exampleCN: 这个体育设施有游泳池。

latinEntries.example: Facere is the root of many English words.
latinEntries.exampleCN: facere 是许多英语词的词根。
